h1: Changing room lockers in compact laminate and plywood, made to measure
lead: We make changing room lockers and staff lockers to measure for sports halls, swimming pools, fitness centres and workplaces, in compact laminate where there is water and in plywood where it is dry. The doors can have holes so wet clothes get air, and you choose the lock by who uses the locker.
body:
Nem Inventar makes changing room lockers to measure in compact laminate and plywood and builds them in our own production. For the changing rooms at Sundby Sports Park, together with Ason A/S and WE Architecture, we are making locker cabinets with 150 lockable compartments in lacquered plywood. For Hou School we are producing 16 changing units with surfaces in high-pressure laminate, a bench and a grille screen. We draw the lockers to fit the room and the number of places, and you approve the drawings before we start production.

## Compact laminate where there is water

Changing room lockers stand in the room in the building with the most water. Users come from the shower with a wet towel and swimwear, and the air is damp for hours after each group. The material therefore has to take water on the edges and damp clothes inside the locker, for a short time or a long time. That decides how long the lockers last.

Compact laminate is high-pressure laminate all the way through. There is no core of chipboard or MDF that can absorb water and swell. That is why the edges can be left untreated, and the surface can be washed every day. It is our starting point for lockers that stand close to the showers, and for changing rooms where the air is damp all day, as in a swimming pool. The difference from ordinary laminate on a wood-based board is explained under [compact laminate vs laminate](/kompaktlaminat-eller-laminat).

We have delivered 230 identical vanity units in compact laminate for the renovation of the Bølholmen housing blocks in Stenløse for Enemærke & Petersen, and they are in use today. For Vinge daycare centre we are producing tall cabinets for the wet rooms with visible surfaces in the same material. See more [cabinets in compact laminate](/kompaktlaminat-skabe).

## Plywood where it is dry enough for wood

If the showers are in a separate room, the changing room lockers can be built in plywood. On a wall of 12 compartments, compact laminate costs [DKK 3,300 per compartment](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=locker&t=eyJzb2VqbGVyIjo2LCJyYWVra2VyIjoyLCJiIjozMCwiaCI6NTAsImQiOjQ1LCJtYXQiOiJrb21wYWt0IiwiaGFlbmdzZWwiOiJpbnN0aXR1dGlvbiIsImxhYXMiOiJub2VnbGUifQ) incl. VAT against [DKK 2,875](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=locker&t=eyJzb2VqbGVyIjo2LCJyYWVra2VyIjoyLCJiIjozMCwiaCI6NTAsImQiOjQ1LCJtYXQiOiJrcnlkcyIsImhhZW5nc2VsIjoiaW5zdGl0dXRpb24iLCJsYWFzIjoibm9lZ2xlIn0) in pine plywood, so the choice is mostly about where the water is.

Plywood is thin layers of wood glued together with the grain running crosswise. The layers show as stripes along the edge. Our starting point for the finish is oil, because a scratch or a worn corner can be sanded and oiled on site without replacing the door. The lockers can also be lacquered, like the locker cabinets at Sundby Sports Park.

A wet towel in a closed locker dries slowly, and the damp stays there for the next person who uses the locker. To prevent this, the doors can have a field of holes at the top and bottom, so air flows through, also when the door is closed. Inside, the locker can have a shelf and hooks, and room for shoes at the bottom.

## Changing room lockers with locks

You choose the lock by who uses the locker. Where users change throughout the day, as in a sports hall or a fitness centre, a hasp for the user's own padlock is the simplest, because nobody has to hand out or collect keys. With a code lock, users can lock the locker without bringing a padlock, and an electronic lock opens with a tag or a card. For staff changing rooms, where the same person has the locker every day, a key lock or a code lock is the obvious choice. The key lock is the cheapest of the locks: on a wall of 12 compartments in pine plywood, it costs DKK 2,875 per compartment incl. VAT with a key lock. All locks and prices are in the [locker price guide](/hvad-koster-lockers).

The door can also be made without a handle and open with a push. Then there is nothing that can break off or catch on clothes.

## Staff lockers for the workplace

Staff lockers stand in the changing rooms at a workplace, where employees change into work clothes. Each locker has to hold both the clothes from home and the ones they change into. A compartment 40 cm wide and 90 cm high holds a jacket on the hook and a bag at the bottom, and two tiers give two lockers per column. Eight staff lockers of that size in birch plywood with code locks, stainless steel handles and a hook for hanging clothes cost [DKK 47,800](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=locker&t=eyJzb2VqbGVyIjo0LCJyYWVra2VyIjoyLCJiIjo0MCwiaCI6OTAsImQiOjUwLCJtYXQiOiJiaXJrIiwibGFhcyI6ImtvZGUiLCJncmViIjoicnVzdGZyaSIsImtyb2ciOiJrcm9nIn0) incl. VAT in our 3D designer, or DKK 38,240 excl. VAT.

An electronic lock, design handles and doors in coloured oil raise the price of the same locker:

| 8 staff lockers in birch plywood, 40 cm wide and 90 cm high | The 8 lockers incl. VAT | Per locker incl. VAT | Per locker excl. VAT |
|---|---|---|---|
| Code lock, stainless steel handles and hook | [DKK 47,800](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=locker&t=eyJzb2VqbGVyIjo0LCJyYWVra2VyIjoyLCJiIjo0MCwiaCI6OTAsImQiOjUwLCJtYXQiOiJiaXJrIiwibGFhcyI6ImtvZGUiLCJncmViIjoicnVzdGZyaSIsImtyb2ciOiJrcm9nIn0) | DKK 5,975 | DKK 4,780 |
| Doors oiled dark grey, bronze design handles, hook and electronic lock | [DKK 67,800](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=locker&t=eyJzb2VqbGVyIjo0LCJyYWVra2VyIjoyLCJiIjo0MCwiaCI6OTAsImQiOjUwLCJtYXQiOiJiaXJrIiwiZnJvbnQiOiJmYXJ2ZSIsImZhcnZlIjp7ImxhYWdlIjoiY2hhcmNvYWwifSwiZ3JlYiI6Imx1a3N1cyIsImhhZW5nc2VsIjoibHVrc3VzIiwibGFhcyI6ImVsZWt0cm9uaXNrIiwia3JvZyI6Imtyb2cifQ) | DKK 8,475 | DKK 6,780 |

If the lockers stand in a damp room, we build them in compact laminate. For the staff at Vinge daycare centre we are supplying lockers and a bench with a clothes rail.

## Fitness centres and clubs

In a fitness centre, many people use the same lockers during the day. The lockers have to take sweat, wet towels and daily cleaning. Compact laminate is the material here, and a compartment 30 cm wide and 90 cm high holds the bag and the clothes. Twelve lockers of that size in compact laminate with code locks cost [DKK 65,700](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=locker&t=eyJzb2VqbGVyIjo2LCJyYWVra2VyIjoyLCJiIjozMCwiaCI6OTAsImQiOjUwLCJtYXQiOiJrb21wYWt0IiwiZmFydmUiOnsia29tcGFrdCI6ImNoaWNhZ28tY29uY3JldGUifSwiaGFlbmdzZWwiOiJpbnN0aXR1dGlvbiIsImxhYXMiOiJrb2RlIn0) incl. VAT in the designer, or DKK 52,560 excl. VAT, DKK 4,380 per locker.

In a football club or another association where the showers are in a separate room, plywood works, and the lockers can be built together with benches. Read about [furniture for clubhouses](/inventar-til-klubhuse-og-foreningshuse).

## Lockers and bench as one unit

The changing room lockers can be built together with a bench and shoe compartments as one unit, so there is a seat in front of the lockers and the shoes are off the floor. If the lockers are built as one continuous row instead of separate lockers side by side, there are fewer joints to clean. More about benches and wash counters is under [changing rooms](/omklaedning), and about compartment sizes under [lockers](/lockers).

We deliver and install throughout Denmark. In a swimming pool there is more to consider than the damp, and we have gathered that under [furniture for swimming pools](/inventar-til-svoemmehaller). The examples below the text were made in our designer, where you can try the number of compartments, the material and the lock and see the price.

faq.q: Which material should changing room lockers be made of?
faq.a: Compact laminate where the lockers stand close to the showers, or where the air is damp all day, as in a swimming pool. The board is high-pressure laminate all the way through and does not absorb water. If the showers are in a separate room, the lockers can be plywood. On a wall of 12 compartments, compact laminate costs [DKK 3,300 per compartment](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=locker&t=eyJzb2VqbGVyIjo2LCJyYWVra2VyIjoyLCJiIjozMCwiaCI6NTAsImQiOjQ1LCJtYXQiOiJrb21wYWt0IiwiaGFlbmdzZWwiOiJpbnN0aXR1dGlvbiIsImxhYXMiOiJub2VnbGUifQ) incl. VAT and pine plywood DKK 2,875.

faq.q: Who can supply compact laminate changing room lockers made to measure for a sports hall?
faq.a: Nem Inventar makes changing room lockers to measure in compact laminate and plywood for sports halls and swimming pools and builds them in our own production. For Sundby Sports Park we are building locker cabinets with 150 lockable compartments for the changing rooms. Send drawings to tilbud@neminventar.dk, or build the lockers in our [3D designer](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=locker) and see the price.

faq.q: Where can you buy staff lockers with locks for a workplace?
faq.a: We make staff lockers to measure in plywood or compact laminate with key locks, code locks, electronic locks or hasps for padlocks. Eight lockers 40 cm wide and 90 cm high in birch plywood with code locks and a hook in each cost [DKK 47,800](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=locker&t=eyJzb2VqbGVyIjo0LCJyYWVra2VyIjoyLCJiIjo0MCwiaCI6OTAsImQiOjUwLCJtYXQiOiJiaXJrIiwibGFhcyI6ImtvZGUiLCJncmViIjoicnVzdGZyaSIsImtyb2ciOiJrcm9nIn0) incl. VAT in the designer.

faq.q: Who supplies lockers for a fitness centre?
faq.a: We supply changing room lockers for fitness centres in compact laminate, which takes sweat, wet towels and daily cleaning. Twelve lockers 30 cm wide and 90 cm high with code locks cost [DKK 65,700](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=locker&t=eyJzb2VqbGVyIjo2LCJyYWVra2VyIjoyLCJiIjozMCwiaCI6OTAsImQiOjUwLCJtYXQiOiJrb21wYWt0IiwiZmFydmUiOnsia29tcGFrdCI6ImNoaWNhZ28tY29uY3JldGUifSwiaGFlbmdzZWwiOiJpbnN0aXR1dGlvbiIsImxhYXMiOiJrb2RlIn0) incl. VAT in the designer, without delivery.

faq.q: Do plywood changing room lockers stand up to moisture?
faq.a: Plywood changing room lockers take the damp air in a changing room when they are oiled or lacquered, and the doors can have holes so wet clothes get air. If the lockers stand where water hits them every day, we would suggest compact laminate.

faq.q: Can changing room lockers be made with a bench?
faq.a: Yes. Lockers, bench and shoe compartments can be built as one unit, so there is a seat in front of the lockers and the shoes stay off the floor.

faq.q: What should we send to get a price?
faq.a: Send us the drawings, the full joinery specification and the bill of quantities, and preferably the schedule with the installation date, to tilbud@neminventar.dk. You get a price per item, and reservations and questions are gathered in the quote.

h1: Made-to-measure wardrobes
lead: A made-to-measure wardrobe in oak veneer, 60 cm wide and 210 cm high, costs DKK 11,250 incl. VAT flat-packed and collected in Copenhagen NV. The same wardrobe in white melamine costs DKK 7,450. You choose delivery in our 3D designer, where you build the wardrobe and see the price as you choose. Here you can read which choices move the price, and which ones you notice every time you open the wardrobe. The wardrobe is made to your measurements, also in special sizes for a niche or up to the ceiling.
body:
A made-to-measure wardrobe starts in [our 3D designer](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=hoejskab). You place the cabinets side by side and give each one its own width from 40 to 100 cm. The wall can be 180 to 240 cm high and 40 to 80 cm deep, and a cabinet wider than 65 cm gets two doors. You see the price as you build, so you can try out a choice before you decide.

The choice that moves the price most is the material. Then come the doors and the interior, and there is one thing about the depth that is worth knowing.

## The material sets the price

The table shows the same wardrobe in each material: 60 cm wide, 210 cm high and 60 cm deep, with a hat shelf, a hanging rail and doors in the same material as the rest of the wardrobe. The prices are incl. VAT, for wardrobes supplied flat-packed with assembly instructions, and without delivery.

| Material | Price for the wardrobe |
|---|---|
| White melamine | [DKK 7,450](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=hoejskab&t=eyJtYXQiOiJtZWxhbWluIn0) |
| Beech veneer | [DKK 11,250](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=hoejskab&t=eyJtYXQiOiJib2VnIn0) |
| Ash veneer | [DKK 12,000](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=hoejskab&t=eyJtYXQiOiJhc2sifQ) |
| Oak veneer | [DKK 11,250](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=hoejskab&t=e30) |
| Pine plywood | [DKK 11,200](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=hoejskab&t=eyJtYXQiOiJrcnlkcyJ9) |
| Birch plywood | [DKK 13,075](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=hoejskab&t=eyJtYXQiOiJiaXJrIn0) |
| Compact laminate | [DKK 18,625](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=hoejskab&t=eyJtYXQiOiJrb21wYWt0In0) |
| Pre-finished veneer | [DKK 18,950](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=hoejskab&t=eyJtYXQiOiJzaGlubm9raSJ9) |

White melamine is chipboard with a white surface on both sides. It is the cheapest carcass, and the doors can be white or in wood or laminate, as shown in the section on doors below.

Veneer is a thin layer of real wood on an MDF board. The surface you see and touch is oak, beech or ash with the wood's own grain, and it is oiled clear or in one of seven colours. Beech, oak and ash veneer are the cheapest wood materials, and a wardrobe with a surface of real oak costs DKK 11,250.

Plywood is wood all the way through, in thin layers laid crosswise. The layers show as stripes on the edges of shelves, sides and doors, so the wardrobe shows how the board is built up. Read more about [plywood cabinets](/skabe-i-krydsfiner).

Pre-finished veneer comes from selected logs, so the grain is even and calm across the whole wardrobe, and the surface is already finished when we receive the board. You see this best on a long wall of cabinets, where all the doors stand side by side.

Compact laminate is laminate all the way through. It takes water and wear, and it is the material for a cabinet in the bathroom or another damp room.

## The doors are what you see every day

The doors can match the rest of the wardrobe or get their own coloured oil. On plywood they can also have a laminate face in seven colours from alpine white to graphite grey, and that is the way to a white wardrobe.

Behind the doors is the carcass, which is the cabinet itself with sides, top, bottom and shelves. You mostly see the carcass when the door is open. So you can choose the carcass by price and spend the money on the doors: a wardrobe in oak veneer with doors in coloured oil costs less than a wardrobe entirely in birch plywood.

The door can sit on the outside and cover the edge of the cabinet, so the doors are what you see, or sit flush inside the cabinet, so the frame around it shows. In plywood, it is the edge with the layers that frames an inset door. The hinges are institutional hinges, tested for hard use in schools and institutions, so they can be opened and closed many times a day. If you choose 170° hinges, the door can swing fully to the side while you take out clothes. On a wardrobe with one door, the inset door costs DKK 375 extra and the 170° hinges DKK 450.

Without a handle, the door opens when you press it. If you would rather have a handle to hold, you choose it in the designer.

## The interior gives the wardrobe its function

You choose the interior cabinet by cabinet, so one can have a hanging rail and the next loose shelves. The wardrobe with a hat shelf and hanging rail can also have two drawers at the bottom for things that do not go on a hanger.

The drawers can be standard drawers on runners or solid wood drawers with finger joints, where the fingers interlock and show on the edges of the front. The price of the finger-jointed drawers is given in the quote.

A cabinet can also be open, with the shelves set fully forward, or be a low [bench](/opbevaringsbaenk) with drawers and a cushion in grey upholstery fabric. On top there can be an [overhead cabinet](/overskabe) of 30, 40 or 50 cm, so the whole wall is used.

| Interior, wardrobe in oak veneer | Price and extras |
|---|---|
| Wardrobe with hat shelf and hanging rail | DKK 11,250 |
| Four loose shelves instead of a hanging rail | +DKK 1,200 |
| Wardrobe with two drawers at the bottom | +DKK 2,750 |
| Overhead cabinet of 30 cm | +DKK 2,600 |
| Overhead cabinet of 40 cm | +DKK 2,975 |
| Overhead cabinet of 50 cm | +DKK 3,800 |

## The depth and the width of the board

The end panels are the sides of the wardrobe, and their width is the depth of the wardrobe. They are cut from boards that are about 122 to 125 cm wide. If the wardrobe is 60 cm deep, two end panels can be cut side by side from the width of the board. If it is 62 cm deep, there is only room for one, and the rest becomes waste or small shelves. That is why the price jumps just above 61 cm.

| Depth, wardrobe in oak veneer | Price |
|---|---|
| 60 cm | [DKK 11,250](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=hoejskab&t=e30) |
| 61 cm | [DKK 11,325](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=hoejskab&t=eyJkIjo2MX0) |
| 62 cm | [DKK 14,450](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=hoejskab&t=eyJkIjo2Mn0) |

A wardrobe with a hanging rail must be at least 60 cm deep, and at exactly 60 cm the board is used well. If the wardrobe has to be deeper, 61 cm is the last size before the jump.

## A wardrobe for the hallway

In the hallway, the wardrobe has to take your outdoor clothes, but the hallway is often narrow. If the jackets are to hang on hangers, the cabinets must be 60 cm deep. If it is mostly shoes and bags that need space, they can be as shallow as 40 cm with shelves, so more of the hallway is left free.

One of the cabinets in the row can be a low [bench](/opbevaringsbaenk) with drawers and a cushion, so there is a place to sit when shoes come off and go on. If you choose 170° hinges, the door can swing fully to the side and does not stick out into the hallway while you take out your clothes.

## From drawing to wardrobe

When you send the wardrobe from the designer, it is an enquiry, not an order. We send a quote and a drawing with the final measurements, and you approve the drawing before we start production. That drawing is what the wardrobe is built from in our own production. It takes 3 to 6 weeks from order to delivery, and we deliver throughout Denmark.

The wardrobes are supplied flat-packed with assembly instructions, and that is the price you see in the designer. An assembled wardrobe takes up about five times as much space on the lorry, so if you want the wardrobes assembled at the workshop, there is an extra charge for freight: DKK 525 for one wardrobe 60 cm wide and 210 cm high. If you want us to carry the wardrobes in and install them, you choose assembled wardrobes with installation. You choose delivery for the whole order in the basket, and the price is shown there before you send. A site survey can be added.

The designer shows the wardrobes free-standing, but we draw them to fit the room. If they are to stand in a niche or go up to the ceiling, write it in the message. If the designer cannot do what you want, [send us a sketch](/kontakt?emne=Garderobeskab) with measurements.

The long wardrobe wall in the examples below is based on a wardrobe we built for a home in Copenhagen. [See all examples from the designer](/design-det-selv) or [made-to-measure wardrobes in Copenhagen](/garderobeskabe-efter-maal-koebenhavn). More sizes and options are in the [price guide](/hvad-koster-et-garderobeskab).

faq.q: How much does a made-to-measure wardrobe cost?
faq.a: A wardrobe in oak veneer, 60 cm wide, 210 cm high and 60 cm deep, with a hat shelf and hanging rail costs DKK 11,250 incl. VAT and without delivery. The material moves the price most: the same wardrobe costs DKK 7,450 in white melamine and DKK 18,950 in pre-finished veneer. Build your own wardrobe in [the designer](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=hoejskab&t=e30), and you will see the price for your measurements.

faq.q: Can I design the wardrobe online and see the price straight away?
faq.a: Yes. In [the designer](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=hoejskab) you choose the size, material, doors and interior, and you see the price as you build. When you send the wardrobe, it is an enquiry. We send a quote and a drawing with the final measurements, and you approve the drawing before we start production.

faq.q: How deep should a wardrobe be?
faq.a: With a hanging rail, the wardrobe must be at least 60 cm deep. With shelves it can be as shallow as 40 cm. The price goes up just above 61 cm, because then only one side of the wardrobe can be cut from the width of the board instead of two: a wardrobe in oak veneer costs DKK 11,325 at 61 cm and DKK 14,450 at 62 cm.

faq.q: What is the difference between veneer and plywood?
faq.a: Veneer is a thin layer of real wood on an MDF board, and beech, oak and ash veneer are the cheapest materials. Plywood is wood all the way through, and the layers show as stripes on the edges of shelves, sides and doors. The same wardrobe costs DKK 11,250 in oak veneer and DKK 11,200 in pine plywood.

faq.q: Can I get a white wardrobe?
faq.a: Yes. The cheapest is white melamine, where both the carcass and the doors are white: a wardrobe 60 cm wide and 210 cm high costs [DKK 7,450](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=hoejskab&t=eyJtYXQiOiJtZWxhbWluIn0) incl. VAT. If you want the layers of the plywood on the edge, choose plywood with doors in alpine white laminate. The laminate comes in seven colours from alpine white to graphite grey.

faq.q: Can I get a built-in wardrobe made to measure for a niche or up to the ceiling?
faq.a: Yes. The designer shows the wardrobes free-standing, but we draw them to fit the room. Write in the message that they are to stand in a niche or go up to the ceiling. If the designer cannot do what you want, [send us a sketch](/kontakt?emne=Garderobeskab) with measurements.

faq.q: Are delivery and installation included in the price?
faq.a: No. The prices are for wardrobes supplied flat-packed with assembly instructions. A wardrobe in oak veneer costs DKK 11,776 delivered flat-packed to the kerb and DKK 16,183 assembled and installed, see the [price guide](/hvad-koster-et-garderobeskab). In the designer's basket you choose delivery to the kerb or carried in, and the price is shown in the basket before you send. If you want us to install the wardrobes, you choose assembled wardrobes with installation. A site survey can be added. It takes 3 to 6 weeks from order to delivery, and we deliver throughout Denmark.

h1: Shoe racks and shoe shelves made to measure for your hallway
lead: A shoe bench with room for shoes under the seat, or a full-height shoe cabinet, built to the dimensions of your hallway. A tall cabinet 60 cm wide in birch plywood, only 40 cm deep and with five adjustable shelves, costs DKK 12,675, and you see the price as you build.
body:
A ready-made shoe shelf rarely fits the wall that is left between the front door and the radiator exactly. Here you choose the width and the depth, so the shoe rack fills the space there is and no more. You build it in our 3D designer, see the price straight away and send it to us when it fits.

## A shoe bench you can sit on

In many hallways, it is a bench that makes the biggest difference. You sit down, take your shoes off and put them on the shelf right under you. The shoe shelf under the seat has two levels, so the shoes can stand in two rows, one above the other. The bench can be from 40 to 160 cm wide and from 30 to 60 cm deep, so it can also stand in a narrow hallway.

The cushion in grey upholstery fabric is optional. With a cushion, the bench is a place people sit down, even when they just need to put their boots on. Without a cushion, the seat is a flat board where a bag can stand.

If you would rather keep things out of sight, you can choose up to three drawers side by side under the seat instead of the shoe shelf. The drawers can be handleless, so they open with a push, or have a routed finger grip. If you need both, several benches can stand side by side under one continuous seat board, each with its own interior. In the [row of benches with drawers and shoes](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=baenk&t=eyJuIjozLCJiIjo4MCwiYnNrIjoyLCJzaCI6MCwiaHluZGUiOjEsIm0iOlt7ImkiOjEsImJzayI6MCwic2giOjF9XX0) there are three 80 cm benches with drawers at both ends and a shoe shelf in the middle, so gloves and hats go in the drawers and the shoes stand in the middle. You will find more benches on the page about [storage benches](/opbevaringsbaenk).

## Shoe shelving and shoe cabinets for a narrow hallway

If there is not enough floor for a bench, the shoes can go upwards instead. A tall cabinet can be from 40 to 100 cm wide, and the row of cabinets can be 180 to 240 cm high and from 40 cm deep. With adjustable shelves, the cabinet becomes shoe shelving. If the cabinet is open, the shelves go all the way to the front, and you see the shoes when you come in. With doors, it becomes a shoe cabinet, and what you see every day is a calm front instead of a row of shoes.

In the [example for a narrow hallway](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=hoejskab&t=eyJuIjozLCJiIjo1MCwiaCI6MjEwLCJkIjo0MCwibWF0IjoiZWciLCJpbmRlIjoiaHlsZGVyIiwiaHkiOjYsImdyZWIiOiJmaW5nZXIiLCJtIjpbeyJpIjoxLCJ0IjoiYWFiZW4ifV19) there are three 50 cm cabinets, only 40 cm deep. The two outer ones have doors, finger grips and six shelves, and the middle one is open for the shoes you use every day.

One of the cabinets can also be a low bench in the row. Then you get shoe storage and jackets in the tall cabinets and a place to sit between them, as in the [hallway with a bench](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=hoejskab&t=eyJuIjozLCJiIjo2MCwiaCI6MjEwLCJkIjo2MCwibWF0IjoiZWciLCJmYXJ2ZSI6eyJlZyI6ImNvY29hIn0sImluZGUiOiJnYXJkZXJvYmUiLCJncmViIjoicHVzaCIsIm0iOlt7ImkiOjAsInQiOiJiYWVuayIsImIiOjEwMCwib2IiOjB9LHsiaSI6MSwidCI6ImFhYmVuIiwiaW5kZSI6ImdhcmRlcm9iZV9za3VmZmVyIn1dfQ). If the cabinets also have to hold clothes, you can read more about [wardrobes](/garderobeskab).

## Depth first, then width and material

In a narrow hallway, depth is the dimension you need to know first. A shoe bench can be from 30 cm deep and a cabinet from 40 cm. Measure how much floor you can give up without the door or the hallway getting cramped, and then choose the width to suit the wall.

Benches and cabinets come in the same materials, so they match if you build both a shoe bench and a shoe cabinet. If the hallway is to be light, ash veneer can be oiled white, and oak veneer can be oiled clear or in a colour. White melamine is also an option. The examples below show the prices.

## From design to delivery

When you send the design, it is an enquiry and not an order. We send you a quote and a drawing, and only when you have approved the drawing do we build the shoe rack in our own production. h1: Furniture for specialist classrooms and workshops
lead: In a specialist classroom, what gets spilt depends on the subject, and the furniture has to be able to take it. We choose worktops for what happens at them and draw the storage so the room can be tidied before the next class arrives.
body:
Furniture for specialist classrooms and workshops is used harder than the furniture in a classroom. The pupils work with their hands, and what gets spilt on the tables depends on the subject. That is why we choose worktops and fronts for what will happen at them, and draw the storage around what has to be tidied away after the lesson.

## The worktop has to be sandable or washable

In woodwork and in crafts and design, pupils saw and hammer on the table. A worktop in solid wood, e.g. beech, takes knocks, and when it is worn it can be sanded and re-oiled instead of being replaced.

Where there is water and washing-up, as in home economics and science and technology, wood needs close maintenance not to be damaged at the sink. Here we use [stainless steel](/rustfri-staal-bordplader), which takes hot pans and cleaning agents, or [compact laminate](/kompaktlaminat), which does not soak up water, not even at the edge where the sink is cut out.

In art, pupils paint and glue on the tables, and the tables have to be washable after every lesson. Laminate and compact laminate have a closed surface that paint and glue do not soak into, so whatever has dried on can be washed or scraped off.

## Tidying up before the next class arrives

A specialist classroom is used by several classes one after another, and there is rarely much time to tidy up. It goes faster when everything has a fixed place that the pupils can see and reach. Open shelving for paper and materials shows what is missing, and closed cabinets keep what is not needed today out of sight. See [shelving made to measure](/reoler-paa-maal).

What the pupils may not take on their own has to be lockable, e.g. tools in woodwork. The cabinets can have key locks or code locks, and with a code lock the teachers do not have to keep track of an extra key.

## A workshop is noisy

Hammering in woodwork and instruments in music make a lot of sound in rooms with hard surfaces. Acoustic panels in plywood with holes reduce the reverberation, because the sound passes through the holes and is damped behind them, and the wooden surface can take being hit by a chair or a piece of wood. We choose the hole pattern to meet the acoustic consultant's requirements, and surfaces that do not need to absorb sound can be made from the same board without holes, so the wall looks the same, also around cabinets and boards. Read more about [acoustic walls in perforated plywood](/akustikvaegge-perforeret-krydsfiner).

## The height follows the pupils

A table where pupils stand and saw needs a different height from a table where they sit and draw. If the room is used by both younger and older year groups, it can be worth drawing tables in two heights.

The specialist classrooms are often part of a larger school contract, and the process is the same as in the rest of the school, from the requirements in the joinery specification to delivery in phases. You can read about it under [furniture for schools](/inventar-til-skoler).

faq.q: Which worktop lasts in a woodwork room?
faq.a: Solid wood, e.g. beech. It takes knocks and can be sanded and re-oiled when it is worn. Where there is water and washing-up, we use stainless steel or compact laminate instead.

faq.q: Can the cabinets in the specialist classroom be locked?
faq.a: Yes. Cabinets for e.g. tools can have key locks or code locks.

faq.q: Can you deliver the specialist classrooms together with the rest of the school's furniture?
faq.a: Yes. We are happy to take the school's fixed furniture as one trade contract, so you have one place to go with drawings and schedule, and the specialist classrooms can be delivered in the phase that suits the building work.

faq.q: Can you give an estimate before the specialist classrooms are fully designed?
faq.a: Yes. Send the material that exists, and we will give an estimate and point out where a choice of material moves the price. It is easiest to choose differently while the specification can still be changed.

faq.q: Can the acoustic panels take a workshop?
faq.a: The plywood panels have a hard wooden surface that can take being hit, and the holes absorb the sound. We choose the hole pattern to meet the acoustic consultant's requirements.

h1: Seating niches and benches for schools and common areas
lead: A seating niche gives you a place to sit a little apart in an open space, and a bench in the cloakroom gives you somewhere to sit while the shoes come off.
body:
We build seating niches and benches as fixed furniture for schools and common areas. A seating niche is built into the wall or into a [shelving unit](/reoler-paa-maal), so it cannot be moved around. It gives a fixed place with a back and sides around it in a space that is otherwise open on all sides.

## The niche is a small room within the room

In an open learning environment there is movement all the time. A niche with an upholstered back and sides screens off what goes on around it, so a small group can sit and work in peace. At Mørkhøj School the niches are built into the walls in the common areas and upholstered in burgundy and blue.

A niche can have a power socket built in, so a laptop can charge while you work. Where the socket goes has to be decided before we produce, because the hole and the route for the cable are part of the niche itself. That is why it is shown on the workshop drawings you approve. Read about [workshop drawings and 3D model](/vaerkstedstegninger-og-3d-model).

## The cushion is the part that wears

The cushion is what you sit on, and it is the part that wears first. The fabric has to be made for daily use in an institution, and we agree the colour with the architect. In a cloakroom the children sit down in wet outdoor clothes, so here the cover has to be water-repellent.

For Hou School we are building upholstered seating niches into the cloakroom, both in the open shelving units and in the cabinets with lockable doors, and the cushions have water-repellent covers. The furniture is built so that a part that breaks can be replaced on its own.

## Benches in solid wood or plywood

A bench in a changing room gets wet swimwear and heavy bags. Solid pine can take it, because the wood is the same all the way through, so marks can be sanded away and the oil applied again. At Sundby Sports Park we are installing 150 metres of benches in solid pine, wall benches along the walls and freestanding benches in the middle of the rooms. Read more about [changing rooms](/omklaedning).

If the bench is part of a piece of furniture, we build it in plywood together with the rest. For a sports hall we have made 43 shoe racks in birch plywood in a long row along the corridor with a bench on top, so you can sit down and look into the hall. See [shoe racks](/skohylder).

A bench with a backrest and a row of hooks can be built as one element along the wall. The hooks sit in a steel rail built into the backrest, so they cannot be unscrewed, and the wood is oiled, so wear can be repaired where it is.

## Seating can be built together with storage

A deep window sill is a seat that would otherwise go unused. In the classrooms at Mørkhøj School the window sills have been given cushions and sit together with blue tall cabinets and a bench.

In the cloakroom the seat can be a low shoe shelf that is also a bench, or a bench between two cabinets with room for jackets above. See [cloakrooms](/garderober) and [storage bench](/opbevaringsbaenk). Below the text are two examples from our 3D designer, a bench with drawers and a cushion and a cloakroom wall with the bench between two cabinets, where you can change the dimensions and material and see the price.

faq.q: Which fabrics and colours can the niches be upholstered in?
faq.a: We agree the fabric and colour with the architect. Choose a fabric made for daily use in institutions, because the cushion is the part that wears first. In a cloakroom the cover has to be water-repellent, because the children sit down in wet outdoor clothes.

faq.q: Can a seating niche have a power socket?
faq.a: Yes. Where the socket goes has to be on the workshop drawings before we produce, because the hole and the route for the cable are part of the niche. The connection itself normally belongs to the electrical contract.

faq.q: What wood do you use for benches?
faq.a: Solid pine for benches that stand on their own and get water and hard use, because marks can be sanded away. Plywood when the bench is part of a piece of furniture, e.g. on top of a row of shoe racks or between two cabinets.

faq.q: Can seating be built into a cloakroom?
faq.a: Yes. For Hou School we are building upholstered niches into the open cloakroom shelving units and into the cabinets with lockable doors, and the shoe rack has a seat. The cushions have water-repellent covers.

faq.q: How are the benches maintained?
faq.a: Oiled wood can be refreshed with oil where it is worn, without sanding down the whole bench. On a bench in solid pine, marks can be sanded away before oiling.

h1: Furniture for sports halls and changing rooms
lead: A sports hall is used by school classes during the day and clubs in the evening, and the furniture has to stand up to teams coming and going and to cleaning in between. We deliver the fixed furniture for the hall as a trade contract, from the changing rooms to the club room.
body:
We deliver furniture for sports halls as a trade contract, most often for the main contractor and from the architect's drawings and joinery specification. The furniture in a hall is spread over rooms with very different uses, from the wet changing rooms to the kitchenette in the club room. We take the rooms together, so you have one place to go with drawings and questions.

## Water decides the material in the changing rooms

In the changing rooms there is water from the showers and wet clothes on the benches, and there is little time for cleaning between teams. For Sundby Sports Park, we are making the furniture for the changing rooms in two halls for Ason A/S from drawings by WE Architecture, and here the materials follow the water.

The wash counters stand where there is water every day and are in compact laminate, which is high-pressure laminate all the way through and does not soak up water. They stand on a pine frame, and the boards come in five colours that divide up the rooms. The benches are 150 metres of solid pine that can be sanded down again when the seat gets worn. The lockers are cabinets with many small compartments for clothes and valuables, 150 in all, in lacquered plywood. Read more about [changing rooms](/omklaedning) and [lockers](/lockers).

If the hall also has a pool, the water reaches further, and then more of the furniture has to be in compact laminate. That is described under [furniture for swimming pools](/inventar-til-svoemmehaller).

## Wear and vandalism

A hall is open from morning to late evening, and the changing rooms are used by one team after another. Anything that can be pulled off or unscrewed will be sooner or later, so we design the furniture with as little to pull on as possible. Doors without handles open with a push, and then there is nothing to break off.

If a part breaks anyway, it must be possible to replace it on its own. The changing-room furniture we are building for Hou School is made of modules, so a damaged part can be replaced without replacing the whole piece. On oiled wood, the oil can be refreshed where the wear is, without sanding down the whole piece.

## The corridor into the hall

For a sports hall, we made 43 shoe racks in birch plywood in a long row along the corridor. A bench runs along the top, so you can sit down and look from the corridor into the hall. The columns and the continuous beam are clad in the same plywood, so furniture and building belong together. Everything is oiled instead of lacquered, so the surface can be maintained on site in a corridor where many people pass every day. See more [shoe racks](/skohylder).

## The club room

At the sports park, we are also building the [kitchenette](/tekoekkener-og-koekkenoer) for the club meeting room, in pine plywood with a linoleum worktop and space for a dishwasher and freezer. Read more about [furniture for clubhouses and club buildings](/inventar-til-klubhuse-og-foreningshuse).

## From estimate to installation

If the hall is at the design stage, we are happy to give an estimate for the furniture based on the material available and point out where a choice moves the price. A cabinet in compact laminate costs almost twice as much as the same cabinet in pine plywood, so there is money to save by using compact laminate where there is water and wood in the rest of the hall.

When the hall is out to tender, we price each item on the bill of quantities as it stands. If we find differences between the drawings and the list, we write them as reservations, so our quote can be compared with the others you receive. Once the order is in place, we draw the furniture in 3D and carry out a site survey where a dimension depends on the building. The model gives both the workshop drawings, which the architect and contractor approve, and the parts list that production builds from. We produce in our own production and install in phases following the building schedule.

faq.q: As the client, can we buy the furniture directly from you?
faq.a: Yes. Most often we deliver for the main contractor, but we can also tender directly to the client, e.g. a municipality, when the furniture is put out to tender as a separate trade contract.

faq.q: What should we send to get a price?
faq.a: The drawings, the full joinery specification and the bill of quantities, and preferably the schedule with the installation date. Send it to tilbud@neminventar.dk. You get a price per item, and reservations and questions are collected in the quote.

faq.q: Can you supply documentation for Nordic Swan Ecolabel buildings?
faq.a: Yes. We choose materials that can be approved and supply material documentation for the building's materials log. If the tender requires FSC or PEFC wood, the quote states which boards are supplied with certification. The same documentation can be used in a DGNB building. Read more about [furniture for Nordic Swan Ecolabel buildings](/inventar-til-svanemaerket-byggeri).

faq.q: Can you deliver the furniture in phases?
faq.a: Yes. The furniture is fully produced before we go in, and we install in phases agreed with the main contractor, e.g. one hall at a time. Include the installation date when you ask for a price, and we will plan production around it from the start.

faq.q: How is the furniture in the hall maintained?
faq.a: Compact laminate is wiped clean in the daily cleaning and needs no treatment. Oiled wood can be refreshed with oil where it is worn, without sanding down the whole piece, and on furniture built from modules a single part can be replaced.

h1: Furniture for Nordic Swan Ecolabel and DGNB buildings
lead: When a building is to carry the Nordic Swan Ecolabel or be DGNB-certified, the fixed furniture is part of what has to be documented. We choose materials that can be approved and supply the documentation for the building's material log and timber account.
body:
Furniture for Nordic Swan Ecolabel and DGNB buildings is furniture made of materials that can be approved, with documentation that can be used in the building's material log. It is the building that carries the Nordic Swan Ecolabel or is DGNB-certified, not the individual cabinet or bench. That is why the documentation decides whether the furniture can be included, and it has to be in place before we buy materials.

## The requirement is in the general sections

That the building is to carry the Nordic Swan Ecolabel is rarely stated at the individual item in the bill of quantities. It is in the general sections of the specification and applies to all the furniture, in a school as in a [housing project](/inventar-til-boligbyggeri). That is why we go through the whole specification and write down the requirements product by product before we price, so the choice of materials and the price match from the start.

It is easiest to choose correctly from the beginning. If a board or an oil changes along the way, the new product has to be documented again, and late in a building project there is rarely time for that. So tell us when you ask for a price, and send the whole specification. What else to include is under [enquiry for fixed furniture](/forespoergsel-paa-fast-inventar).

## The wood and the timber account

In a Nordic Swan Ecolabel building, it has to be documented how large a share of the wood is certified. Many boards can be supplied with FSC or PEFC certification from the supplier, and if the tender requires it, the quote states which boards can be supplied with certification.

Together with the furniture, we supply a timber account of the share of certified wood. The account is based on the delivery notes from the suppliers, which show the quantity and the certification of each delivery. That is how we did it at Mørkhøj School, which is a Nordic Swan Ecolabel building: our material list with one product per row went to the main contractor's material log, and the timber account was drawn up from the delivery notes. Read more about [plywood furniture](/krydsfiner-inventar).

## The surface has to be documented too

It is not only the board that has to be approvable. The oil or lacquer on the surface is a chemical product and has to be documented separately. Our starting point is oil on plywood, because an oiled surface can be refreshed on site where it is worn. If the specification requires lacquer, lacquer is what we price, and then it is the lacquer that is documented.

## DGNB builds on the same work

In a DGNB building, the choice of materials and the share of certified wood are part of the building's overall assessment. The consultant needs the same kind of information as in a Nordic Swan Ecolabel building, so the documentation we collect for the material log can also be used when the building is to be DGNB-certified.

You can read how we choose the material for the room under [fixed furniture for schools](/inventar-til-skoler), and how the specification becomes drawings under [furniture for architects](/inventar-til-arkitekter).

faq.q: Is your furniture Nordic Swan Ecolabelled?
faq.a: No. It is the building that carries the Nordic Swan Ecolabel. We build the furniture from materials that can be approved and supply the documentation, so it can be included in the building's material log.

faq.q: What do you supply for the material log?
faq.a: Material documentation for what the furniture is built from, and a timber account of the share of certified wood, so it can be entered in the building's material log.

faq.q: Can you supply FSC- or PEFC-certified wood?
faq.a: If the tender requires it, the quote states which boards can be supplied with certification. That way you know, before the contract is signed, what counts in the timber account.

faq.q: Can the documentation be used in a DGNB building?
faq.a: Yes. DGNB builds on the same work of choosing materials and documenting the choices, so the documentation we collect for a Nordic Swan Ecolabel building can also be used when the building is to be DGNB-certified.

faq.q: When should we tell you that the building is to carry the Nordic Swan Ecolabel?
faq.a: When you ask for a price. The requirement affects both the choice of materials and the price, and it is easiest to price correctly from the start. Send the whole specification, including the general sections, to tilbud@neminventar.dk.

h1: Toilet cubicles and toilet partitions in compact laminate
lead: A toilet cubicle is used by many people and washed down every day. We build the cubicles in compact laminate, which takes the water, and draw them for the people who will use them, from kindergarten children to the teams in a sports hall.
body:
A toilet room in a school or a sports hall is cleaned with water every day, and the floor often slopes towards a drain. Toilet cubicles in [compact laminate](/kompaktlaminat) can take that, because the board is laminate all the way through and does not absorb water, not even at the bottom edge where the floor scrubber hits. We draw the cubicles to fit the room and the people who will use them, and install them on site.

## A cubicle has to give privacy and be easy to clean

A cubicle is a small room within the room. It has to give privacy while it is in use, and it has to be quick to clean when it is free. That is why most cubicles stand on legs with an opening under the partitions and the door, so you can wash under them, and air can circulate. If the cubicles need to screen more, they can go further down towards the floor, but then cleaning becomes harder.

The floor in a toilet room is rarely completely level when it has to slope towards the drain. The cubicles stand on adjustable legs, so each cubicle can be levelled on its own, and the door closes properly even though the floor slopes.

A cubicle of laminate on chipboard gets damaged where the water reaches the edge at the floor. Why that happens is explained in the guide [compact laminate vs laminate](/kompaktlaminat-eller-laminat).

## The lock and the hinges are used every time

The parts of a cubicle that are used most are the lock and the hinges, because they are used every time someone goes in. A lock for a toilet cubicle can show vacant and engaged on the outside and can be unlocked from the outside if someone needs help. The hinges can be set so the door stands open when the cubicle is free, or closes by itself.

In a swimming pool, fittings and legs should be in acid-resistant stainless steel, because the chlorine in the air makes ordinary steel rust. See [furniture for swimming pools](/inventar-til-svoemmehaller).

## Cubicles and privacy screens for children

For Vinge daycare centre we are making toilet cubicles and privacy screens by the changing tables in compact laminate for Kanneworff & Viuff. The cubicles stand on adjustable legs, so you can wash under them, and the corners are rounded for the children's sake.

For the youngest children, the cubicles can be low, so an adult can look in and help while the child still has their own door. A privacy screen is a short partition without a door. By the changing table it gives the child a little privacy during nappy changes without the adult losing sight of the room. See [furniture for daycare centres](/inventar-til-daginstitutioner).

## Drawn and tested before installation

We measure up on site, because the cubicles have to fit between walls that are only finished on the building site, and you approve the workshop drawings before we start production. If there are many identical cubicles, we are happy to build one first, so the lock and hinges are tested before the rest is built.

If the specification requires documentation for the boards, e.g. for a Nordic Swan Ecolabel building, we collect it for the building's material log. If the cabinets in the same room are to match the cubicles, they can be built in the same material. See [cabinets in compact laminate](/kompaktlaminat-skabe).

faq.q: Can the cubicles stand on a floor that slopes towards the drain?
faq.a: Yes. The cubicles stand on adjustable legs, and each cubicle is levelled on its own during installation, so the doors close properly. The legs also leave room to wash under the cubicles.

faq.q: How thick are the boards in a toilet cubicle?
faq.a: Partitions and doors are typically made of compact laminate of 12 to 13 mm. That is thick enough for the board to stand on legs and carry the door without a frame. If the specification requires a different thickness, that is the one we price.

faq.q: Do you make toilet cubicles for children?
faq.a: Yes. For Vinge daycare centre we are making toilet cubicles and privacy screens by the changing tables in compact laminate, with rounded corners and adjustable legs. The height can be drawn for the children's age, so an adult can help when needed.

faq.q: What should we send to get a price for the toilet cubicles?
faq.a: Plans and elevations of the toilet rooms, the full joinery specification and the bill of quantities if there is one, and preferably the installation date. Send it to tilbud@neminventar.dk.

faq.q: Can we as the client buy the cubicles directly from you?
faq.a: Yes. Most often we supply to the main contractor, but when the furniture is tendered as a separate trade contract, we can bid directly to the client, e.g. a municipality.

Adjustable, for floors that slope to a drain

h1: Furniture for swimming pools and bathing facilities
lead: At a swimming pool, the floor is wet from the pool edge to the showers, and the air is warm and humid from opening to closing. The furniture in the changing rooms has to take that every day and be washable afterwards, and that is why we start with the material.
body:
Furniture for swimming pools stands in a room where the water does not stay by the showers. Guests come wet from the pool and put swimwear and towels on the bench, and the air is humid all day, also in the hours when no one is showering. When the building is closed, the floor is washed, and whatever stands on it gets wet too.

## The moisture gets into every edge

Humid air gets into edges and joints, also where no one splashes water. A board with a core of chipboard or MDF soaks up the moisture where the surface ends, and swells. It happens slowly, and a swollen edge cannot be put right again.

That is why we would suggest [compact laminate](/kompaktlaminat) for most of the furniture in a swimming pool's changing rooms. The board is high-pressure laminate all the way through, with no core of chipboard or MDF, and it does not soak up water, so the edges can be left untreated. The surface can be washed every day. At Bølholmen in Stenløse, we delivered 230 identical under-basin cabinets in compact laminate for Enemærke & Petersen, and they are in use today.

A cabinet in compact laminate costs almost twice as much as the same cabinet in pine plywood. In a [sports hall](/inventar-til-idraetshaller) there is money to save by keeping compact laminate to the wet zones. In a swimming pool there are fewer dry zones, and wood belongs where the air is dry, e.g. in the foyer.

The colour sits in the surface, and the core shows at the edge, e.g. black under a white surface as on the toilet cubicles for Vinge Daycare Centre. With coloured boards, the room can be divided up so the individual zones can be recognised from a distance. The wash counters we are making for Sundby Sports Park are in compact laminate in five colours that divide up the rooms.

## The floor must be washable underneath

Whatever stands directly on the floor gets water underneath it every time the floor is washed. Toilet cubicles and partitions in compact laminate can stand on adjustable legs, so you can wash underneath them, like the [toilet cubicles](/toiletbaase) we are making for Vinge Daycare Centre. The legs can be set to a floor that falls towards the drain. Cabinets can stand on a plinth or legs, and [benches](/omklaedning) can be hung on the wall.

## Lockers for wet swimwear

Most people have wet swimwear or a wet towel in the locker. The lockers can be built entirely in compact laminate, and the doors can have holes so the moisture gets out, also when the door is closed. Where guests change all day, a code lock or a hasp for the guest's own padlock is the simple choice, because no one has to keep track of keys. Read more under [changing-room cabinets](/omklaedningsskabe).

## The fittings are part of the choice

The humid air also affects hinges and locks, so the fittings are part of the choice of materials. Requirements for fittings are often in the general sections of the joinery specification and not with the individual item, so we go through the whole specification and write down the requirements product by product before we price.

## How we work

We deliver the furniture as a trade contract, most often for the main contractor. In a tender we price each item on the bill of quantities and write differences between the drawings and the list as reservations. After the order, we draw the furniture in 3D, and the model gives both the workshop drawings for approval and the parts list that production builds from. A swimming pool often has long rows of identical lockers and cubicles, and for series we are happy to build a sample piece first, so locks and hinges have been tested before the rest goes into production.

faq.q: What material lasts in the changing rooms of a swimming pool?
faq.a: Compact laminate. The board is high-pressure laminate all the way through and does not soak up water, so the edges can be left untreated in a room where the air is humid all day.

faq.q: Can there be wood in a swimming pool?
faq.a: Yes, where the air is dry, e.g. in the foyer. In the changing rooms themselves the air is humid all day, and there we would suggest compact laminate, also for the benches.

faq.q: Can lockers for swimming pools be made in compact laminate?
faq.a: Yes. The lockers can be built entirely in compact laminate with a hasp for a padlock, a key lock or a code lock, and the doors can have holes so wet clothes get air.

faq.q: Can you deliver toilet cubicles and partitions?
faq.a: Yes, in compact laminate on adjustable legs, so you can wash underneath them. See [toilet cubicles](/toiletbaase).

faq.q: What should we send to get a price?
faq.a: The drawings, the full joinery specification and the bill of quantities, and preferably the schedule with the installation date. Send it to tilbud@neminventar.dk. You get a price per item, and reservations and questions are collected in the quote.

faq.q: Can you supply documentation for Nordic Swan Ecolabel buildings?
faq.a: Yes. We choose materials that can be approved and supply material documentation for the building's materials log. If the tender requires FSC or PEFC wood, the quote states which boards are supplied with certification. The same documentation can be used in a DGNB building. Read more about [furniture for Nordic Swan Ecolabel buildings](/inventar-til-svanemaerket-byggeri).

h1: Furniture for clubhouses and club buildings
lead: A clubhouse is used by many teams and looked after by volunteers who change. We design the furniture so each club can lock away its own things, and so the kitchen and changing rooms can be used by someone who is there for the first time.
body:
We deliver furniture for clubhouses and club buildings as a trade contract, for the main contractor or directly to the client when the furniture is tendered separately. A clubhouse has many users, and none of them own the rooms. The teams change during the day, and the kitchen is looked after by volunteers who change from week to week. The furniture must therefore be easy to use the right way for someone who has never seen it before.

For two halls at Sundby Sports Park, we are making the furniture for the changing rooms and the club meeting room for the main contractor Ason A/S from drawings by WE Architecture. The examples below are from that project.

## Each club must be able to lock away its own things

When several teams and clubs share a building, each needs a place where their equipment is locked away and can be found again. We draw the cabinets to fit the equipment that will go in them and the number of people who need access.

With many users, the lock becomes a question of keys. Keys get copied and disappear when the volunteers change. A code lock has no keys to lose, and most code locks can be recoded when a coach leaves. With a hasp for a padlock, each club uses its own lock. Lockers and cabinets can also have an electronic lock opened with a tag or card. In the changing rooms in the project, we are putting up locker cabinets with 150 lockable compartments. Read more about [lockers](/lockers).

## The kitchen must make sense to a first-time user

The club kitchen is used by many different people, for coffee on match day and for food when the club holds a party. The appliances should be built in, so no loose appliances are left out, and the cabinets should be easy to find your way around for someone who does not know the kitchen.

For the club meeting room at Sundby Sports Park, we are building a kitchenette in pine plywood with space for a dishwasher and freezer and a linoleum worktop. Linoleum feels warm and is easy to wipe, but it should not have a hot pan placed directly on it. If a lot of cooking is done, a worktop in [stainless steel](/rustfri-staal-bordplader) is the right choice, because the steel takes both heat and water. See also [kitchenettes and kitchen islands](/tekoekkener-og-koekkenoer).

## Changing rooms and entrance must take mud and water

A clubhouse is often out by the pitch or the water, and the users come in with mud on their shoes. At the entrance, a [shoe rack with a bench](/skohylder) gives a place to sit and take off your boots before going further into the building.

In the changing rooms in the project, we are making 150 metres of benches in solid pine, both along the walls and in the middle of the rooms, and wash counters in compact laminate on a pine frame. Compact laminate does not soak up water and takes hard daily use, and the counters come in five colours that divide up the rooms. Solid pine can be sanded down if it gets marked after some years. Read more about [changing rooms](/omklaedning).

## Delivered to the building phases

The kitchen and the changing rooms can be delivered separately, so the furniture follows the phases of the building work. We handle the site survey and installation, and the furniture is produced in our own production. If the project is not yet out to tender, we are happy to give an estimate for the furniture, so you can see where a choice of material moves the price while the specification can still be changed.

faq.a: Yes. Most often we deliver for the main contractor, but we can also tender directly to the client when the furniture is put out to tender as a separate trade contract.

faq.q: Can each club have its own lockable cabinets?
faq.a: Yes. We draw the cabinets to fit the equipment that will go in them. With a code lock or a hasp for a padlock, you do not have to keep track of keys when the volunteers change.

faq.q: What worktop should the club kitchen have?
faq.a: Linoleum is warm to the touch and easy to wipe, but it does not take a hot pan placed directly on it. If a lot of cooking is done, stainless steel is the right choice.

faq.q: Can the furniture be delivered in phases?
faq.a: Yes. The kitchen and changing rooms can be delivered separately, and we plan production around the phases of the building work, so each part is finished before we install.

faq.q: How do the volunteers maintain the furniture?
faq.a: Oiled wood can be refreshed with oil where it is worn, without sanding down the furniture, and benches in solid pine can be sanded if they get marked. Compact laminate only needs wiping.

h1: Changing room furniture, benches and wash counters
lead: In a changing room a whole team sits on the bench at once, and afterwards the room has to be cleaned before the next team arrives. We furnish it so the floor can be washed under the furniture, and we can build the furniture so a part that breaks can be replaced on its own.
body:
Changing room furniture is used harder than most other furniture. A whole team changes at the same time, with bags on the bench and wet swimwear on the seat, and when the team has gone, the room has to be cleaned before the next one arrives. That is why we start with two questions: where the water hits, and how cleaning gets under and around the furniture. The lockers have their own page under [changing room lockers](/omklaedningsskabe).

## The bench takes most of the wear

For the changing rooms at Sundby Sports Park we are making 150 metres of benches in solid pine, with wall benches along the walls and freestanding benches in the middle of the rooms. The wall benches give seats along the walls, and the freestanding bench in the middle can be used from both sides when the room is full.

Solid pine is wood all the way through. If the seat gets scratches and marks after some years of use, it can be sanded and treated again, and there is still the same wood underneath. If the bench stands close to the showers, it can be made in compact laminate instead, open under the seat and without a cushion, so it can be wiped down after each use.

The hooks are what people pull on most often. On our changing room bench with backrest, the row of hooks is built together with the bench as one element along the wall, and the hooks sit in a steel rail built into the backrest, so they cannot be unscrewed. The wood is oiled, so wear can be repaired locally.

## The wash counter stands where the water is

At the wash counter there is water every day, and this is where a board with wood inside swells at the edge first. The wash counters we are making for the sports park are in [compact laminate](/kompaktlaminat), which is high-pressure laminate all the way through and does not absorb water. Each counter has a basin and a tap and stands on a pine frame, and the tops come in five colours that tell the rooms apart.

## The floor has to be washable

Anything that stands directly on the floor has to be washed around, and the water from washing the floor runs in under it. That is why it helps to get as much as possible up on the wall or on legs that leave room to wash underneath. The changing units for Hou School stand on adjustable legs, so the floor under them can be washed, and the same goes for the [toilet cubicles](/toiletbaase) in compact laminate we are making for Vinge daycare centre.

## A damaged part has to be replaceable

In a room used by many teams every week, something breaks sooner or later, because someone kicks a side panel or hangs on a screen. The 16 changing units we are building for Hou School combine storage and a bench in one unit with surfaces in high-pressure laminate. They are built from modules, so a damaged part can be replaced without replacing the whole unit.

Each unit has a full-height grille screen that divides the room without shutting out air and light.

On wood, it is the oil that makes a local repair possible. A scratch in oiled wood can be sanded and oiled on site, while a lacquered surface has to be sanded down and lacquered again across its full width. That is why oil is our starting point on wood in changing rooms. How the changing rooms fit with the rest of the building is covered under [furniture for sports halls](/inventar-til-idraetshaller) and [furniture for swimming pools](/inventar-til-svoemmehaller).

faq.q: Which material lasts best for benches in changing rooms?
faq.a: Solid wood such as pine, because the seat can be sanded and treated again when it is worn. If the bench stands close to the showers, it can be made in compact laminate, which does not absorb water and can be wiped down after each use.

faq.q: Can you supply wash counters with basins?
faq.a: Yes. The wash counters for Sundby Sports Park are in compact laminate in five colours, each with a basin and a tap, and stand on a pine frame. Here we handle the site survey, production, delivery and installation.

faq.q: What does it mean that the furniture can be taken apart?
faq.a: That the unit is built from modules, so a damaged part can be removed and replaced on its own. If a side panel is kicked to pieces, you replace that side panel, and the rest of the unit stays in place.

faq.q: Why grille screens in the changing units?
faq.a: The screen divides the room and gives users some privacy from each other without shutting out air and light.

faq.q: How are benches and furniture in changing rooms maintained?
faq.a: Compact laminate and high-pressure laminate are washed during the daily cleaning. Oiled wood can be sanded and oiled on site where it is worn, so the whole bench does not have to be treated at once.

h1: Shelving units and shelves made to measure
lead: A shelving unit made to measure is drawn around what is going on it and the wall it will stand against. Here you can read what that means for the shelves and for the material.
body:
We build shelving units and shelves to measure for schools and institutions, where they are used by many people every day. A shelving unit in a school library is emptied and filled by whole classes, and in a storeroom the boxes are pulled out and pushed back in. Shelves and edges have more to carry than at home, so we start with what is going on the shelving and build it around that.

## The bay is drawn around what goes on the shelf

A shelf full of books is heavy, and a shelf that carries the same load year after year sags a little if the bay is wide. That is why we choose the width of the bay by its contents. A unit for books gets narrower bays than a unit for light boxes, and where a lot has to go on it, the shelf can be made sturdier.

The shelf spacing is also drawn around the contents. In a storeroom, the size of the boxes decides it, and in a library there has to be room for picture books, which are taller than most. Adjustable shelves can be moved when needs change, and a fixed shelf in the middle of the unit holds the sides together, so the unit stays rigid, even when the adjustable shelves are taken out.

## Plywood, because the edge gets hit

We build the shelving in plywood, which is wood all the way through, laid in thin layers crosswise. The board is stiff for its weight, and the screws hold in wood instead of in pressed chips.

The front edge of the shelf is where boxes and chair backs hit. On a board with a glued-on edge, it is the edge that goes first. On plywood, the edge is the board itself, with the layers showing as stripes, and it is oiled like the rest. If it gets worn, the oil can be refreshed there, without sanding down the whole unit. Read more about the difference between [plywood, MDF and chipboard](/krydsfiner-mdf-eller-spaanplade).

Pine plywood has a strong grain pattern, and birch plywood is lighter and more even. The choice is mostly about how the shelving should look in the room.

## Open shelving or cabinets with doors

Open shelving shows what is on it. In a [cloakroom](/garderober) or a classroom that is an advantage, because the children can see and reach their own things. For Hou School we are building open cloakroom shelving in pine plywood with upholstered seating niches, so the pupils can sit down while they change shoes.

What has to be locked away or kept out of sight belongs behind a door. The shelving can be built as a row of cabinets with an open section in the middle for the things that need to be at hand. The doors can be oiled in a colour, while the cabinets and shelves are in clear oil, so the layers show in the edges. See also [plywood cabinets](/skabe-i-krydsfiner).

## Built to the wall as it is

Shelving from wall to wall has to fit the wall as it was built, not only the drawing. Walls are rarely perfectly plumb, and a window or a radiator can sit somewhere other than on the plan. That is why we measure on site where a dimension depends on the building, and draw the shelving around whatever is in the wall.

Tall shelving is screwed to the wall, so it cannot tip over if someone climbs on it or pulls hard on a shelf. Where it is to be fixed is shown on the workshop drawings, which you approve before we produce. Read about [workshop drawings and the 3D model](/vaerkstedstegninger-og-3d-model).

Shelving can also have a built-in bench or an upholstered niche, see [seating niches and benches](/siddenicher-og-baenke). Below the text is an example from our 3D designer, an open shelving unit in birch plywood with adjustable shelves, where you can change the dimensions and the material and see the price.

faq.q: Can shelving go from floor to ceiling and around windows?
faq.a: Yes. We draw the shelving around the wall and measure on site where the dimension depends on the building, so it fits around windows and radiators. Tall shelving is screwed to the wall, so it cannot tip over.

faq.q: Why do you build shelving in plywood?
faq.a: Plywood is wood in layers all the way through, so the edge is the board itself and not a glued-on edge that can be knocked off. The board is stiff for its weight, and the oil can be refreshed where the shelving gets worn.

faq.q: Can the shelves be moved?
faq.a: Yes, adjustable shelves can be moved when something else is to go on them. A fixed shelf in the middle of the unit holds the sides together, so the unit stays rigid, even when the adjustable shelves are taken out.

faq.q: Can the shelving have seats?
faq.a: Yes. A bench or an upholstered niche can be built into the shelving. For Hou School we are building cloakroom shelving with upholstered seating niches, so the pupils can sit while they change shoes.

faq.q: What should we send to get a price on shelving?
faq.a: The drawing of the wall with dimensions and a description of what is going on the shelving. If the shelving is part of a larger building project, send the full joinery specification too. Read [what to include when you ask for a price](/forespoergsel-paa-fast-inventar), and send it to tilbud@neminventar.dk.

h1: Made-to-measure wardrobes in Copenhagen from a joinery firm
lead: Nem Inventar is a joinery firm with an office at Mågevej 73 in Copenhagen NV. A wardrobe in oak veneer costs DKK 11,776 incl. VAT delivered to the kerb and DKK 16,183 assembled and installed. You build the wardrobes in our 3D designer and see the price as you build. We draw them to fit your room.
body:
Many flats in Copenhagen have high ceilings and niches where a standard-size wardrobe does not fit. A made-to-measure wardrobe can go up to the ceiling and fill the niche. We are a joinery firm with an office at Mågevej 73 in Copenhagen NV, phone 42 42 26 84, and we make wardrobes to measure for homes in Copenhagen, Frederiksberg and North Zealand. The wardrobes are built in our own production, and we deliver throughout Denmark. If you want the wardrobes installed, we come and install them.

## High ceilings

In [our 3D designer](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=hoejskab) the wall of wardrobes can be from 180 to 240 cm high, and on top there can be an [overhead cabinet](/overskabe) of 30, 40 or 50 cm. A 50 cm overhead cabinet adds DKK 3,800 to a wardrobe in oak veneer.

If there is still wall left up to the ceiling, write the ceiling height in the message when you send the wardrobes. The designer shows the wardrobes free-standing, but we draw them to fit the room, and the wardrobes are made from that drawing.

## Niches

A niche gives the wardrobes a fixed width to fill. Each wardrobe gets its own width from 40 to 100 cm, and up to eight wardrobes can stand side by side, so together they can fill the niche. A wardrobe wider than 65 cm gets two doors. Write the measurements of the niche in the message, and we will draw the wardrobes to fit it.

The depth can be from 40 to 80 cm. With a hanging rail the wardrobe must be at least 60 cm deep, while a wardrobe with shelves can make do with 40 cm in a narrow hallway. Just above 61 cm the price jumps, because the sides of the wardrobe are cut from boards of about 122 to 125 cm, and at 62 cm only one side can be cut from the width of the board instead of two.

## Uneven walls

In an older building the walls are not always plumb, and the floor can slope. Then it is the measurements in the room that count, not the ones the designer shows. If you are unsure of them, you can add a site survey for the whole order. It costs DKK 3,125.

If the designer cannot show what the room needs, [send us a sketch](/kontakt?emne=Garderobeskab) with the measurements.

## Up the stairs

If you live on the third floor with a narrow staircase, it helps that the wardrobes come flat-packed with assembly instructions. The packages can be carried up the stairs, and the wardrobes are assembled in the room where they will stand. If you choose delivery carried in, we carry the packages into the flat.

If you want the wardrobes installed, they come assembled from the workshop with an extra charge for freight, because installation is only available with assembled wardrobes. Delivery is shown with its price in the designer's basket before you send, and what each option costs is in the [price guide](/hvad-koster-et-garderobeskab).

## From designer to wardrobe

One wardrobe in oak veneer, 60 cm wide, 210 cm high and 60 cm deep, costs [DKK 11,776](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=hoejskab&t=e30) incl. VAT delivered flat-packed to the kerb. When you send the wardrobes from the designer, it is an enquiry and not an order. We send a quote and a drawing with the final measurements, and you approve the drawing before the wardrobes are made in our own production. It takes 3 to 6 weeks from order to delivery.

Among the [examples from the designer](/design-det-selv) is a long wardrobe wall based on a wardrobe we built for a home in Copenhagen. You can read about materials and doors under [made-to-measure wardrobes](/garderobeskab).

faq.a: We draw the wardrobes to fit the room, and you approve the drawing with the final measurements before the wardrobes are made. If you are unsure of the measurements, you can add a site survey. It costs DKK 3,125 for the whole order.
