h1: Glass boards and acoustic panels for teaching rooms
lead: In the classroom, the same wall has to work for writing and for absorbing sound. We draw glass boards and acoustic panels as one wall, to the room's dimensions and the acoustician's report.
body:
Glass boards and acoustic panels belong together in a teaching room. The teacher needs to write and show things, and the pupils need to hear what is said, also at the back. That is why we plan the boards and the acoustic panels as one wall, drawn to the room's dimensions, so the boards sit where the teaching happens and the panels where the acoustician's report places them.

## Glass absorbs almost no sound

A glass board is a hard surface, and glass reflects almost all the sound. If the board wall faces another hard wall, the sound can bounce back and forth between the two, so the room rings when someone speaks. That is why the acoustics are part of the job when the board wall is drawn. Whether it is the back wall or the surfaces next to the boards that should absorb sound, and how much, is set out in the acoustician's report.

## Toughened glass that wipes clean

The glass boards are made of toughened safety glass. If the glass breaks, it falls into small pieces instead of sharp shards, which is why glass can be used in a room with children. The surface is dense, so marker does not soak in, and the board can be wiped clean again and again.

Next to the glass boards there can be pinboards for things that need to stay up for weeks, so the glass is free for teaching.

## Textile acoustic panels between the boards

Textile acoustic panels are upholstered: an acoustic board on a rigid backing board, covered with acoustic textile. The soft surface takes in the sound wherever it hits, and because the panels are sewn and built to measure with no minimum quantity, they can follow the widths of the boards and fit above the cabinets.

In a classroom the fabric wears first where the pupils can reach it. If it gets worn, or the wall needs a different colour, the cover is replaced while the panel stays on the wall. We agree the colour with the architect, and shades can be mixed so the panels follow the room's colours.

If the wall gets hit by balls and chairs, e.g. in a common area where pupils play at break time, a panel in perforated plywood is the better choice. The difference between the two is explained under [acoustic panels](/akustikpaneler).

## The ceiling matters more than the wall

The Danish Building Regulations require the reverberation time in a classroom to be at most 0.6 seconds in every octave band from 125 to 4000 Hz, and at most 0.4 seconds in rooms for group work. At 125 Hz the value may be 20 % higher. The requirement applies to the whole furnished room, and the ceiling is one of the largest surfaces. In our calculation of a typical classroom with panels in perforated plywood, the room meets the requirement with an acoustic ceiling, also without panels on the wall. With a hard ceiling, panels on the wall alone do not meet the requirement in the same room, not even when they cover the whole of the largest wall, and the room is furthest from the requirement in the bass, where the panels absorb least.

The calculation is based on publicly available measurements and typical table values, not on measurements of our own panel or of a real room. How it is made is explained under [calculating sound absorption](/beregning-af-lydabsorption), and the classroom is calculated in full under [acoustic walls in perforated plywood](/akustikvaegge-perforeret-krydsfiner). In the [acoustic designer](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=akustik) you can enter your own classroom's dimensions and ceiling and see the reverberation time without and with an acoustic wall in plywood.

## Drawn in 3D and delivered in stages

We draw the board wall in 3D together with the rest of the classroom furniture, from the architect's drawings. The workshop drawings come from the model, and the architect and contractor approve them, so boards and panels fit the wall and each other before anything goes into production. See [workshop drawings and 3D model](/vaerkstedstegninger-og-3d-model).

At Mørkhøj School we are delivering the fixed furniture for the main contractor Ason A/S, to drawings by Rønnow Arkitekter. For the classrooms we have delivered board walls with glass boards and pinboards, 68 glass boards in total, and approx. 300 m² of textile acoustic panels absorb sound in classrooms and common areas. The installation walls at the school, approx. 100 m², are clad, so the services sit behind a calm surface. The furniture is delivered in stages to the site programme, and the first stage has been handed over and is in use. Read more about [fixed furniture for schools](/inventar-til-skoler).

faq.q: What glass do you use for the glass boards?
faq.a: Toughened safety glass. If it breaks, it falls into small pieces instead of sharp shards. The surface is dense, so the board can be wiped clean again and again.

faq.q: Can glass boards and acoustic panels be on the same wall?
faq.a: Yes. We draw the boards and the acoustic panels as one wall to the room's dimensions. Glass absorbs almost nothing, so how much acoustic treatment goes on the board wall, and where the rest goes, follows the acoustician's report.

faq.q: Can textile acoustic panels be placed where pupils can reach them?
faq.a: Yes. The fabric wears first where pupils can reach it, so the cover can be replaced while the panel stays on the wall. If the wall gets hit by balls and chairs, perforated plywood is the better choice.

faq.q: Do we need an acoustician for the classrooms?
faq.a: Yes. For educational buildings it must be documented that the reverberation time meets the limit values in the Danish Building Regulations, and the acoustician's calculation of the room is the basis for how much acoustic treatment is needed and where it goes. We draw the panels to the report, and the reverberation time is measured in the finished room.

faq.q: Can you supply documentation for Nordic Swan Ecolabel buildings?
faq.a: Yes. We supply material documentation for the building's materials log and a timber account of the share of certified wood. If the tender requires FSC or PEFC wood, the quote states which boards are supplied with certification. Read more about [furniture for Nordic Swan Ecolabel buildings](/inventar-til-svanemaerket-byggeri).

h1: Cloakrooms and children's cloakroom units for schools and institutions
lead: A cloakroom is used by the whole group at once. We draw it to fit the room and the number of users, so each one has their own space and a place to sit when shoes go on.
body:
Cloakrooms in schools and daycare centres are used by the whole group at once, several times a day. What decides whether a cloakroom works is therefore how many people can use it at the same time without getting in each other's way. We draw the cloakrooms to fit the room and the number of users, so there is a space for each one and a place to sit when shoes go on.

## One space each, and a colour to find it by

When a whole group has to put on outdoor clothes at the same time, it goes faster if each child has their own space and knows where it is. For Vinge Daycare Centre we are making 92 children's cloakroom units, in Danish often called troldegarderober, with one module per child. The hooks sit at the top, and the base is deeper with a shoe grille, so shoes and boots can drip dry without standing in water.

The modules are oiled in red and blue, so the rows are divided up and the children quickly learn their own space. The rest of the daycare centre's furniture is described under [furniture for daycare centres](/inventar-til-daginstitutioner).

## A seat keeps the cloakroom clear

Someone standing on one leg pulling on a boot blocks the way for the next. That is why we like to build the seating into the cloakroom itself. For Hou School we are building cloakrooms in pine plywood, where the open shelving units have upholstered seating niches, so pupils can sit to change shoes or pack their bag with their own things within reach. The cushions have water-repellent covers, because they are sat on in wet rainwear.

At Mørkhøj School the pupils' lockers stand with a bench and shoe racks, so shoes and outdoor clothes are kept in one place. Read more about [seating niches and benches](/siddenicher-og-baenke) and [shoe racks](/skohylder).

## Open shelving or closed cabinet

An open cloakroom is quicker to use than a cabinet. The child can see their things and reach them without help, and there are no doors to open and close while others wait.

A closed cabinet gives a place to lock away a phone or a wallet. At the same school, the cloakroom cabinets have lockable doors and an upholstered niche, so locked storage and seating are combined in one piece of furniture. At Mørkhøj School the locker doors have holes, so the clothes get air even when the door is closed, and code locks, so there are no keys to keep track of.

You can build lockers in our 3D designer and see the price as you go, and the example at the bottom of the page can be used as a starting point. See also [lockers](/lockers).

## When a part breaks

The cloakrooms for Hou School are built so a single part can be replaced if it breaks, without replacing the whole piece of furniture. The wood is oiled instead of lacquered, so a worn surface can be refreshed on site. Read more about [plywood](/krydsfiner-inventar).

## Drawn and tested before production

We draw the cloakrooms in 3D from the architect's drawings, and you approve the workshop drawings before we produce. With many identical modules, we like to build a sample piece first, so the joints and fittings are tested before the rest goes into production. See [workshop drawings and 3D model](/vaerkstedstegninger-og-3d-model).

faq.q: What is a troldegarderobe?
faq.a: A Danish term for a children's cloakroom unit with one space per child, with hooks for outdoor clothes at the top and a deeper base for shoes and boots, often with a shoe grille so they can drip dry. It is the type we are making for Vinge Daycare Centre.

faq.q: Can the cloakrooms be made in the architect's colours?
faq.a: Yes. We use coloured oil, and the colour is agreed with the architect. The oil lets the structure of the wood show through the colour, and two colours can be used to divide up the rows.

faq.q: How do we stop wet shoes and boots from damaging the cloakroom?
faq.a: The base can be made deeper than the rest of the module and get a shoe grille, so the shoes drip dry over the grille. The wood is oiled, so a surface that has become worn can be refreshed on site.

faq.q: Can the cloakroom have lockable cabinets?
faq.a: Yes. Cloakroom cabinets and lockers can have code locks, so there are no keys to keep track of, or fittings for the user's own padlock.

faq.q: What should we send to get a price on the cloakrooms?
faq.a: The drawings and the whole joinery specification, including the general sections, and feel free to write how many people will use each cloakroom. If you have a bill of quantities, we price each item on it. Send it to tilbud@neminventar.dk.

faq.q: Can the cloakrooms be delivered in stages?
faq.a: Yes. We plan production around the building's stages, so each stage is finished before we go in and install.

h1: Fixed furniture for renovation and conversion
lead: When a building is renovated, it is often in use at the same time. We survey the rooms as they are today, and the furniture is finished before we go in, so each room is closed for as short a time as possible.
body:
Fixed furniture for renovation and conversion has to fit rooms that already exist, often in a building where people are teaching or living while the work goes on. It is the use of the building that decides how we plan the work: how long a room can be closed, and when noise is allowed.

## We measure the room as it is today

The drawings of an older building rarely match reality exactly. The walls are not always plumb, and pipes and radiators sit where they were put many years ago. That is why we measure on site and draw the furniture to the dimensions the room has now, not to the old drawings.

In the 3D model we see where the furniture has to go around a pipe, and it is shown on the workshop drawings you approve before we produce. If the floor is not level, a cabinet or a toilet cubicle can stand on adjustable legs that are set on site, so the legs take up the unevenness. The legs also leave room to wash the floor underneath.

## Wet rooms that have to be back in use

Toilets and bathrooms are the rooms that are hardest to do without during the works, and the ones where the furniture gets the most water and cleaning. Here we use [compact laminate](/kompaktlaminat). The board is laminate all the way through and does not soak up water, so the edges can be left untreated, and a cubicle partition or a cabinet can take being washed every day. Read more about [toilet cubicles](/toiletbaase).

For the renovation of the housing blocks at Bølholmen in Stenløse, we have delivered 230 identical under-basin cabinets in compact laminate for 220 homes for the main contractor Enemærke & Petersen. The cabinets are delivered and in use. You can read about series in housing under [furniture for housing](/inventar-til-boligbyggeri).

## Finished before we go in

In a building that is in use, it is the days with a closed room that people notice. That is why the furniture is fully made in our own production before we go in, and the work in the building is installation. That means fewer days of noise and dust in the building. The same applies to a [kitchenette](/tekoekkener-og-koekkenoer) or a cloakroom that is to be replaced.

We plan the phases with the main contractor and the people who use the building, e.g. one floor at a time or during a holiday, so each room is closed for as short a time as possible. At a school, the holidays can decide the order. Read more about [fixed furniture for schools](/inventar-til-skoler).

## The old furniture has to go somewhere too

A renovation has items that a new build does not. The old furniture has to be taken down, and once it is gone, there are often holes and unpainted surfaces left on the wall behind it. We agree who does what on each project, and what we have not priced is stated in the quote, so it does not fall between two contracts. You can read how we write the quote under [furniture for main contractors](/inventar-til-hovedentreprenoerer).

faq.q: Can you install while the building is in use?
faq.a: Yes. The furniture is finished before we go in, and we install in phases agreed with the main contractor and the users of the building, e.g. one floor at a time or during a holiday.

faq.q: How do you make sure the furniture fits an old room?
faq.a: We measure on site and draw to the dimensions the room has today. The workshop drawings show where the furniture goes around pipes and services, and you approve them before we produce.

faq.q: Who takes down the old furniture?
faq.a: We agree that on each project. If the removal is not part of our work, we write it in the quote, so it is clear which contract it belongs to.

faq.q: Can new toilet cubicles stand on a floor that is not level?
faq.a: Yes. The compact laminate cubicles can stand on adjustable legs that are set on site. The legs also leave room to wash the floor under the cubicles.

faq.q: What should we send when the drawings are old?
faq.a: Send the drawings you have and a description of what needs to be done. Photos of the rooms as they look today help with the price. We take the measurements ourselves on site before we draw. Send it to tilbud@neminventar.dk.

h1: Stainless steel worktops and sinks
lead: A stainless steel worktop takes hot pans and daily cleaning and is the obvious choice where food is cooked every day. We build the cabinets underneath to fit the room, so worktop and cabinets fit together from the start.
body:
A stainless steel worktop takes hot pans and a lot of cleaning, and the surface does not absorb anything. That is why steel is the obvious choice in staff kitchens, [club kitchens](/inventar-til-klubhuse-og-foreningshuse) and food technology classrooms, where the worktop is used hard and has to be cleaned quickly. We build cabinets and fronts to fit the room, and the steel top is made to the same dimensions, so the whole kitchen comes from us.

## Why steel where food is cooked

Steel is dense and has no joints where water and food scraps can settle. The sink can be welded into the top, so there is no edge between sink and worktop, and the back edge can be bent up against the wall, so water does not run down behind the cabinets. Those are the two places where a worktop in wood or laminate is most often damaged.

Steel scratches. The scratches do not damage the top, but they show, and after a while the surface turns matt where it is used most. A brushed finish makes the scratches less visible. If the kitchen is mostly used for coffee and lunch, a worktop in linoleum or laminate is often a better choice, because it is warmer to look at. See [kitchenettes and kitchen islands](/tekoekkener-og-koekkenoer).

## The top is made to the final dimensions

A worktop in wood or laminate can be cut to size on site. A steel top cannot, once the edges are bent and the sink is welded in, so the dimensions have to be right before it is made. We measure on site where the worktop has to fit between walls, and draw the kitchen in 3D, so the cabinets and appliances fit under the worktop. You approve the workshop drawings before we go into production.

The position of the sink and the dishwasher is on the drawing, so the cabinets underneath have room for pipes and drain, and the hole for the tap sits in the right place in the steel top.

## The cabinets under the steel

The worktop is the surface that is used hardest, but the fronts are what you see. The fronts can be plywood, oiled in the colour the room needs. The steel takes the use, and the fronts give the room its colour.

If the kitchen is in a utility room or a cleaning room where things are rinsed with water, fronts and base cabinets can be [compact laminate](/kompaktlaminat), which does not swell when water reaches the edges. In a specialist classroom, we draw the kitchen around what will happen in lessons and what has to be locked away. See [furniture for specialist classrooms](/inventar-til-faglokaler).

faq.q: When should we choose a stainless steel worktop?
faq.a: When the kitchen is used for cooking and washing up every day, and the worktop has to take hot pans and a lot of cleaning. For a kitchenette that is mostly used for coffee and lunch, linoleum or laminate is often enough.

faq.q: Can the sink be in one piece with the worktop?
faq.a: Yes. The sink can be welded into the steel top, so there is no joint between sink and worktop. It is the solution that is easiest to keep clean.

faq.q: Can you supply the whole kitchen and not just the worktop?
faq.a: Yes. We build base cabinets, tall cabinets and fronts to fit the room, and the worktop is made to the same dimensions. The kitchen is drawn in one 3D model, and you approve the workshop drawings before we go into production.

faq.q: Does a stainless steel worktop scratch?
faq.a: Yes, and the scratches show. Over time the surface turns matt where it is used most, and a brushed finish makes the scratches less visible. The scratches do not change the fact that the top takes water and heat.

faq.q: What should we send to get a price?
faq.a: The drawings of the kitchen, the joinery specification and the bill of quantities, and tell us which appliances are to be built in. Send it to tilbud@neminventar.dk.

h1: Kitchenettes and kitchen islands for schools and institutions
lead: We draw the kitchenette to fit the room and choose the worktop and fronts for what will happen at it. The kitchen island can stand on wheels, so it can be moved.
body:
We build kitchenettes to measure for schools and institutions, in the staff room or out in the common area. A kitchenette here is used in short bursts by many people at once, in the lunch break or after a meeting, and it is wiped down with whatever is closest to hand. The worktop takes most of it, so we choose that first.

## The worktop is chosen for what happens at it

Stainless steel takes hot pans and standing water, and a sink can be welded into the worktop, so there is no joint where dirt collects. It is the worktop for a kitchen where nobody is in charge of looking after it. Read more about [stainless steel worktops and sinks](/rustfri-staal-bordplader).

Linoleum is made from linseed oil and natural fillers. The surface is matt and warm to the touch, and small scratches do not show as clearly as on a glossy worktop. It should not have a hot pan put directly on it, and the joint at the sink has to be sealed. It suits a kitchen where people make coffee and packed lunches. At Sundby Sports Park we are making the kitchenette for the club meeting room in pine plywood with a linoleum worktop.

Compact laminate is laminate all the way through. The board does not soak up water, and the edges can be left untreated, so it lasts where water stands. An ordinary laminate worktop has laminate on a chipboard core. It is easy to clean, but if water gets in at the cut-out for the sink, it is the core that swells. See [compact laminate vs laminate](/kompaktlaminat-eller-laminat).

## The cabinets are drawn around the appliances

If the appliances are to be built in, we draw the cabinets around the exact models that will go there. A built-in dishwasher or fridge has its own dimensions for the niche and for how air gets to it, and the dimensions are not the same from brand to brand. That is why it helps to know the appliances before we draw. The kitchenette at Sundby Sports Park has room for both a dishwasher and a freezer.

Who supplies the appliances and sink, and who connects water and drainage, is a boundary between the contracts. We write it into the quote, so none of it is forgotten.

The cabinet under the sink is where a leak shows first. Here the bottom can be made of compact laminate, which does not swell if a hose starts to leak. That is the same reason we have made 230 under-basin cabinets in compact laminate for the homes at Bølholmen in Stenløse for Enemærke & Petersen.

The fronts are what you see. In plywood with coloured oil, the kitchenette gets the same look as the rest of the furniture, and the oil can be refreshed where the fronts wear, at the handles and at the bottom. At Mørkhøj School the kitchenettes in the common areas have fronts in blue-oiled plywood, like the school's tall cabinets. Laminate fronts are wiped clean and suit a kitchen that needs a particular colour.

## A kitchen island that can be moved

A kitchen island on wheels suits a room that is used for several things. For Vinge Daycare Centre we are making a mobile kitchen island in pine plywood with a linoleum worktop for the staff. It can be wheeled to where it is needed and pushed aside when the room is cleaned or a meeting is held.

An island on wheels has neither water nor drainage, so it is a place to chop and set things out. If the island needs a sink, it is built as a fixed unit.

The kitchenette is drawn in 3D together with the rest of the furniture, so sockets and water end up in the right places before we produce. Read about [workshop drawings and 3D model](/vaerkstedstegninger-og-3d-model) and about furniture for [clubhouses and club buildings](/inventar-til-klubhuse-og-foreningshuse) and [daycare centres](/inventar-til-daginstitutioner).

faq.q: Can the kitchenette have built-in appliances?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us as early as possible which models they are, because the cabinets are drawn for exactly those. A built-in dishwasher or fridge has its own dimensions and its own requirements for how air gets to it.

faq.q: Which worktop should we choose?
faq.a: Stainless steel where food is cooked and nobody looks after the worktop. Linoleum where people make coffee and packed lunches, and where you want a matt, warm surface. Compact laminate where water stands.

faq.q: Can the kitchen take water at the sink?
faq.a: It depends on the worktop. Stainless steel and compact laminate take standing water. On a laminate worktop it is the cut-out for the sink that has to be sealed, because the core swells if it gets wet. The bottom of the cabinet under the sink can be made of compact laminate.

faq.q: Can a kitchen island on wheels have a sink?
faq.a: No, an island on wheels has neither water nor drainage. It is a place to chop and set things out. If the island needs a sink, it is built as a fixed unit.

faq.q: How are the fronts maintained?
faq.a: Fronts in oiled plywood can be refreshed with oil where they wear, without sanding down the whole front. Laminate fronts are wiped clean.

Plywood with coloured oil, or laminate
Cabinets drawn around the models that will go there
Compact laminate where water stands
On wheels and without water, moved as needed

h1: Fixed furniture for schools
lead: Furniture in a school is used by whole classes at a time and cleaned every day. We choose the material for the room it will stand in, and you approve the drawings before we produce and deliver in phases following the building schedule.
body:
We deliver the fixed furniture for schools as a trade contract, most often for the main contractor and from the architect's drawings and joinery specification. In a school there are many items spread over many rooms. We take them together, so you have one place to go with drawings, questions and schedule.

## Built for pupils and daily cleaning

In the cloakroom, a whole class stands at once with wet boots and heavy bags, and the wear settles at floor level and by the hooks. Here our starting point is oiled plywood, because the oil can be refreshed where the wear is, without sanding down the furniture. Read more about [cloakrooms](/garderober) and [lockers](/lockers).

In toilets and changing rooms we use [compact laminate](/kompaktlaminat). The board is laminate all the way through, does not soak up water and can be washed every day.

In the classroom, the wall has to take writing and absorb sound at the same time. The glass boards are in toughened safety glass, which breaks into small pieces if it shatters, and the fabric covering on the acoustic panels can be replaced without replacing the panel. See [acoustics and glass boards](/akustik-og-glastavler).

A specialist classroom has to take glue, paint and water, so we design it around what will happen in the room and what needs to be locked away. See [furniture for specialist classrooms](/inventar-til-faglokaler).

For Hou School, we are building 16 changing-room units that each combine storage and a bench. They are built so a part that breaks can be replaced on its own, and they stand on adjustable legs, so the floor underneath can be washed.

## The price can be calculated before the specification is locked

If the school is at the design stage, we are happy to give an estimate for the furniture based on the material available and point out where a choice moves the price. It is easiest to choose differently while the specification can still be changed.

The material moves the price the most. A cabinet in compact laminate costs almost twice as much as the same cabinet in pine plywood, so there is money to save by using compact laminate where there is water and plywood in the rest of the school.

When the project is out to tender, we price each item on the bill of quantities as it stands. If we find differences between the drawings and the list, we write them as reservations instead of correcting the list, so our quote can be compared with the others you receive. What we have not priced is also stated in the quote, so nothing falls between two contracts.

## The requirements are often in the general sections of the specification

Requirements for surfaces, fittings and materials are often in the general sections of the joinery specification and not with the individual item. That is why we go through the whole specification and write down the requirements product by product before we price, and check the quote against them again before it is sent. Our starting point is oil on plywood, but if the specification calls for lacquer, lacquer is what we price and deliver.

If the school is to carry the Nordic Swan Ecolabel, we choose materials that can be approved and collect the documentation for the building's materials log. If the tender requires FSC- or PEFC-certified wood, the quote states which boards can be supplied with certification. The same documentation can be used when the building is to be DGNB-certified. Read more about [furniture for Nordic Swan Ecolabel buildings](/inventar-til-svanemaerket-byggeri).

## Drawn in 3D and approved before we produce

Once the order is in place, we draw the furniture in 3D from the architect's drawings and carry out a site survey where a dimension depends on the building. The model gives both the workshop drawings, which the architect and contractor approve, and the parts list that production builds from. If a dimension changes, we correct the model, and the drawings and parts list follow, so no one builds from an old drawing.

For series with many identical elements, we are happy to build a sample piece first, so joints, locks and hinges have been tested before the rest goes into production. Read more about [workshop drawings and the 3D model](/vaerkstedstegninger-og-3d-model).

## Delivered in phases while building or teaching goes on

A school is rarely finished all at once, and during a conversion the pupils often go to school in the meantime. We produce the furniture in our own production and plan production around the phases, so it is finished before we go in. We agree the phases with the main contractor, e.g. one wing at a time or during a holiday, so each room is occupied for as short a time as possible. You can read more about conversions under [furniture in renovation projects](/inventar-ved-renovering).

At Mørkhøj School, we are delivering the fixed furniture for the main contractor Ason A/S from drawings by Rønnow Arkitekter, including 342 lockers with shoe racks and 68 glass boards. Every room was drawn in 3D and approved before it went into production, and the furniture is delivered in phases following the site schedule. The first phase has been handed over and is in use.

faq.q: Can you deliver the furniture in phases while the school is in use?
faq.a: Yes. The furniture is fully produced before we go in, and we install in phases agreed with the main contractor and the school, e.g. one wing at a time or during a holiday. That way each room is occupied for as short a time as possible.

faq.q: What should we send to get a price?
faq.a: The drawings, the full joinery specification and the bill of quantities, and preferably the schedule with the installation date. Send it to tilbud@neminventar.dk. You get a price per item, and reservations and questions are collected in the quote.

faq.q: Can you give an estimate before the project goes out to tender?
faq.a: Yes. Send the material you have, and we will give an estimate for the furniture and point out where a choice of material or a detail moves the price. The material moves it the most, and it is easiest to choose differently before the specification is locked.

faq.q: Can you supply documentation for Nordic Swan Ecolabel buildings?
faq.a: Yes. We choose materials that can be approved and supply material documentation for the building's materials log and a timber account showing the share of certified wood. If the tender requires FSC or PEFC wood, the quote states which boards are supplied with certification. The same documentation can be used in a DGNB building.

faq.q: What do you do when the furniture gets worn or breaks?
faq.a: Oiled wood can be refreshed on site without sanding down the whole piece, and the fabric covering on the acoustic panels can be replaced on its own. We are also happy to build the furniture so a single part can be replaced without replacing the whole piece, as in the changing-room units for Hou School.

faq.q: How long does it take from order to delivery?
faq.a: It depends on the scope and on when the building needs the furniture. Include the installation date when you ask for a price, and we will plan production around it from the start. If it is delivered in phases, we plan production around them.

faq.q: As the client, can we buy the furniture directly from you?
faq.a: Yes. Most often we deliver for the main contractor, but we can also tender directly to the client, e.g. a municipality, when the furniture is put out to tender as a separate trade contract.

h1: Kitchens, wardrobes and bathroom cabinets for housing projects
lead: In a housing project, the same cabinet comes back in home after home. We draw each type once and are happy to build a sample piece, which you approve before the series goes into production.
body:
Furniture for housing means a few types made many times over. The kitchen and the cabinets come back in every home, spread over a few unit types and their mirrored versions, in social housing and blocks of flats, new build and renovation alike. That changes what matters. A mistake on one drawing becomes a mistake in every home of that type, and a choice of material or dimension is multiplied by the number of homes.

## The bathroom and the kitchen

In the bathroom we use compact laminate. The board is solid high-pressure laminate and does not soak up water, so the edges can be left untreated, and the cabinet takes the moisture and the daily cleaning. For the renovation of the housing blocks at Bølholmen in Stenløse, we delivered 230 identical under-basin cabinets in compact laminate for 220 homes for the main contractor Enemærke & Petersen. The cabinets are in use today. Read more about [cabinets in compact laminate](/kompaktlaminat-skabe).

The kitchen is not washed down like a bathroom, and here other materials can do the job. We build the kitchen wall in high-pressure laminate with a laminate worktop, or with doors in stained plywood, where the grain and the edge show. In social housing, the kitchen and cabinets have to last through several tenants and a refurbishment every time a tenant moves out, so the surface has to take cleaning and be possible to restore. See also [plywood cabinets](/skabe-i-krydsfiner).

The examples below were made in our 3D designer for wardrobes, where you can try materials and doors on a wardrobe wall.

## Small choices are multiplied

In a series, the material moves the price the most, and it can be chosen room by room. The dimensions matter too. Plywood boards are just over 120 cm wide, so a plywood cabinet that is 60 cm deep gets two sides out of the width of the board. If it becomes a few centimetres deeper, there is only room for one, and the rest becomes waste or small parts.

On a couple of hundred cabinets, that is worth looking at before the dimension is locked. If the project is still at the design stage, we are happy to give an estimate and point out where a material or a dimension moves the price.

## Each type is drawn once

We draw each type in 3D, and the model gives both the workshop drawings for approval by the architect and contractor and the parts list that production builds from. If a dimension changes on a type, we correct it in one place, and the drawings and parts list follow for all the homes where that type is used. Read more about [workshop drawings and the 3D model](/vaerkstedstegninger-og-3d-model).

Before the series goes into production, we are happy to build a sample piece of the type. This is where you see the door and the surface on a real cabinet, and where a correction costs only one cabinet. When the sample piece is approved, we produce the series in our own production from the same drawing.

## Delivered in step with the stairwells

We plan delivery around the site schedule, e.g. stairwell by stairwell or floor by floor, as the homes become ready for furniture. That way the furniture does not take up space on site and risk being damaged before it goes in. We take the furniture as a trade contract under the main contractor and install it, so the responsibility for product and installation sits in one place. See [furniture for main contractors](/inventar-til-hovedentreprenoerer).

If the building is to carry the Nordic Swan Ecolabel or be DGNB-certified, we supply the material documentation for the building's materials log, see [furniture for Nordic Swan Ecolabel buildings](/inventar-til-svanemaerket-byggeri). You can read about working in buildings that stay in use in the meantime under [furniture in renovation projects](/inventar-ved-renovering).

faq.q: Can you deliver stairwell by stairwell?
faq.a: Yes. We plan delivery around the site schedule, so the furniture arrives when the stairwell is ready for it and does not take up space on site.

faq.q: Do you make a sample piece before the series?
faq.a: Yes, gladly. We build a sample piece of the type, which is approved before the rest goes into production. Corrections after the sample are made in the 3D model, so the drawings and parts list follow.

faq.q: What material do you use for bathroom cabinets?
faq.a: Compact laminate. The board does not soak up water and takes daily cleaning. It is the material in the 230 under-basin cabinets we delivered for 220 homes at Bølholmen in Stenløse.

faq.q: What should we send to get a price?
faq.a: Drawings of the unit types, the full joinery specification and the bill of quantities with the number of each type, and preferably the schedule. Send it to tilbud@neminventar.dk, and you will get a price per item with the reservations collected in the quote.

faq.q: Can you give an estimate before the specification is locked?
faq.a: Yes. Send the material you have, and we will point out where a material or a dimension moves the price. In a series, even small differences are multiplied by the number of homes.

faq.q: Do you also handle installation?
faq.a: Yes. We install the furniture to the plan agreed with the main contractor, so the responsibility for product and installation sits in one place.

h1: Phone lockers for schools with a compartment for each phone
lead: When the school collects phones during school hours, each pupil needs a compartment that can be locked. We make phone lockers in plywood with 30 small compartments that hang on the wall by the classroom, and a cabinet with hasps for padlocks costs DKK 37,500 incl. VAT in our 3D designer.
body:
Nem Inventar makes phone lockers, also called phone storage lockers, to measure in plywood for schools. A phone locker is a narrow locker cabinet with many small compartments, one for each pupil's phone. It hangs on the wall by the entrance to the classroom. We build the cabinet in our own production to suit the size of the class. You can try the number of compartments, the locks and more in our [3D designer](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=locker&t=eyJzb2VqbGVyIjozLCJyYWVra2VyIjoxMCwiYiI6MjYsImgiOjE2LCJkIjoyOCwibWF0Ijoia3J5ZHMiLCJzb2trZWwiOiJ1ZGVuIiwibGFhcyI6ImhhZW5nZWxhYXMifQ).

## A compartment for each pupil

Many schools collect phones during school hours. It works best when each pupil has their own compartment, so the phone does not lie in a box with the others, and nobody is in doubt about whose it is. The standard version has 30 compartments in three columns of ten, and each compartment is 26 cm wide, 16 cm high and 28 cm deep. That is enough room for a phone and a charger, and the compartments can be made larger in the designer if there also has to be room for a wallet and keys.

The phone locker has no plinth and is fixed to the wall, e.g. by the entrance to the classroom, so pupils put their phone away when they come in.

## The lock

Each door has a chrome turn lock with an eye for a padlock, so the door is opened and locked in the same place. The doors can also have key locks or code locks, so pupils lock with a code and nobody has to keep track of keys.

The prices were calculated in our designer and do not include delivery and installation.

## Plywood in the classroom

The phone locker is built in plywood with visible edge layers and oiled in clear oil or in one of our colours, so it can match the lockers and the rest of the furniture in the classroom. The oil can be spot-repaired, so a scratch does not need a new door.

The cabinet is built like the locker cabinets with small lockable compartments that we are making for the changing rooms at Sundby Sports Park, with overlay doors and a padlock per compartment. The photos are from a delivery of that type of cabinet. For Mørkhøj School we are delivering [342 lockers](/lockers) with code locks and shoe shelves. A phone locker can be drawn to match the pupils' lockers.

## From drawing to installation

We draw the phone locker to suit the size of the class, and if the school has several classes, we work out a cabinet for each. We deliver throughout Denmark, and with installation we put the cabinets up on the wall. [Send us the number of classes and pupils](/kontakt?emne=Mobilskab), and we will work out the price. Read also about [lockers](/lockers) and [the price of lockers](/hvad-koster-lockers).

h1: Lockers for hotels, spas and fitness centres, made to measure
lead: We make lockers and changing room cabinets to measure for hotels, spa and wellness facilities, fitness centres and golf clubs, in compact laminate and birch plywood, with electronic locks and installation. In our 3D designer, 12 lockers in black compact laminate with electronic locks cost DKK 80,262.50 incl. VAT, delivered and installed.
body:
Nem Inventar makes lockers and changing room cabinets to measure for hotels, spa and wellness facilities, fitness centres and golf clubs. We draw them in 3D to fit the room, build them in our own production and install them throughout Denmark. For the changing rooms at Sundby Sports Park we are supplying locker cabinets with 150 lockable compartments, and for the renovation of the Bølholmen housing blocks in Stenløse we have delivered 230 cabinets in compact laminate for wet rooms for Enemærke & Petersen, which are in use today.

## The changing room is part of what the guest sees

In a spa or a fitness centre, the lockers stand where the guests change, so they have to take moisture and daily cleaning and also suit the rest of the interior. Compact laminate is laminate all the way through and does not absorb water, so the edges can be left untreated close to the showers, and the surfaces can be washed every day. It comes in several colours, e.g. black, light grey and light concrete. Where it is dry, the lockers can be in birch plywood, which is light and has an even surface, with doors oiled in a colour.

## Electronic locks and no keys to lose

Where guests change all day, a code lock is simple. The guest chooses a code, and there is nothing to hand out. The lockers can also have an electronic lock that opens with a tag or a card, or a hasp for the guest's own padlock. The door can be without a handle and open with a push, or it can have handles that suit the rest of the room. Inside, the compartment can have a coat hook and a shelf, and the doors can have holes so wet clothes and towels get air.

## Staff changing rooms

The staff at the hotel or the centre also need to change. Staff lockers 40 cm wide and 90 cm high hold a jacket, a uniform and a bag, and two tiers give two lockers per column. They can be in compact laminate in wet rooms and in plywood where it is dry. Read more about [changing room and staff lockers](/omklaedningsskabe).

## Golf clubs and clubhouses

In a golf club or a clubhouse, members often keep their own locker all year round. A key lock or a code lock fits here, and tall compartments in birch plywood with a coat hook have room for clothes and shoes. The lockers can be built together with benches, so there is a seat in front. Read about [furniture for clubhouses](/inventar-til-klubhuse-og-foreningshuse).

h1: Furniture for daycare centres and kindergartens
lead: The furniture in a daycare centre has to suit the youngest children and take being washed every day. We choose the material room by room, from the cloakroom to the nappy-changing room, and deliver it all as one trade contract.
body:
We deliver furniture for daycare centres as a trade contract, most often for the main contractor and from the architect's drawings. For Vinge Daycare Centre, we are making the fixed furniture for cloakrooms, toilets, nappy-changing rooms and staff rooms for the contractor Kanneworff & Viuff, and the examples from the cloakroom, the toilets and the staff room below are from that project.

A nursery or a kindergarten makes different demands from a school. The users are small and are helped with their clothes and changed by adults, and most rooms are washed every day. That is why we choose the material by what happens in the room, and the heights follow the children and adults who will use it.

## The cloakroom is where the day starts and ends

In the morning and in the afternoon, the cloakroom is full of children and parents at the same time, and in winter the snowsuits come in wet. The cloakrooms in the project have one module per child and are oiled in red and blue, so the children quickly learn where their place is. How the modules are built is explained under [cloakrooms](/garderober) and [shoe racks](/skohylder).

The colour is in the oil, so the structure of the wood shows through it. If a surface wears by the hooks or at the bottom, the oil can be refreshed where the wear is, without sanding down the whole module.

## Toilets and nappy-changing rooms must be washable everywhere

In the toilets and at the changing tables, cleaning is done with water and cleaning agents every day. Here we use compact laminate, which is laminate all the way through. The board does not soak up water, not even at the edges, so it does not swell from being washed.

The toilet cubicles stand on adjustable legs, so the floor underneath can be washed, and the corners are rounded for the children's sake. At the changing tables we put up screens in the same material, so there is some privacy while a child is being changed. The tall cabinets in the wet rooms get visible surfaces in compact laminate, so the whole room can be cleaned the same way. Read more about [toilet cubicles](/toiletbaase).

## The adults work in the building all day

The staff need a place for their own things that is not part of the children's cloakroom. In the project we are making lockers for the staff and a bench with a clothes rail, so the adults' outdoor clothes have their own place. For the staff there is also a mobile kitchen island on wheels, which can be moved to wherever it is needed. See [kitchenettes and kitchen islands](/tekoekkener-og-koekkenoer).

## A room with many children is noisy

Many children in a room with hard surfaces give a long reverberation time, and then it becomes hard to hear each other. An acoustic wall in plywood with holes reduces the reverberation, because the sound passes through the holes and is absorbed in the layer behind. The holes can also form a motif, e.g. waves, so the wall is also good to look at. The example at the bottom of the page is from our 3D designer, where you can draw the panel with your own hole pattern and see the price as you go. Read more about [acoustic walls in perforated plywood](/akustikvaegge-perforeret-krydsfiner).

## Delivered and installed in one go

All the furniture for Vinge Daycare Centre is produced in our own production and installed together in one go, so you have one delivery to plan around. If the building work is split into phases, we plan production around them.

If your daycare centre is to carry the Nordic Swan Ecolabel, we choose materials that can be approved and collect the documentation for the building's materials log. Read more about [furniture for Nordic Swan Ecolabel buildings](/inventar-til-svanemaerket-byggeri).

h1: Lockers for offices with flexible desks, built to measure
lead: When employees do not have their own desk, they need somewhere to lock away a bag, a jacket, a laptop and so on. We make office lockers to measure in birch and pine plywood. They can have code locks or electronic locks. You can see the price in our 3D designer.
body:
Nem Inventar makes lockers for offices with flexible desks and activity-based offices. The lockers are built to measure in birch or pine plywood in our own production, so they fit the room and the rest of the interior. We draw them in 3D before we build them. In our [3D designer](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=locker) you choose the number of compartments, the sizes, the material, the doors and the lock, and see the price straight away.

## A locker instead of a fixed desk

In an office with flexible desks, employees clear the desk when the day is over. The locker is where the laptop, the charger, the bag and the papers that should not be left out stay overnight. That gives tidy desks and a fixed place for each employee, even when the seats at the desks change from day to day.

The compartment has to be deep enough for a bag and tall enough for what has to stand upright. A compartment 35 cm wide and 45 cm high holds a bag and a laptop. Two tiers give two places per column. If the jacket is to hang in the locker too, a compartment 40 cm wide and 90 cm high has room for a coat hook above the bag.

## The lock follows the way you work

If employees have the same locker every day, a code lock is simple. Nobody has to hand out or collect keys, and the code is the same every morning. The lockers can also have an electronic lock that opens with a tag or a card, a key lock or a hasp for a padlock.

## The lockers have to suit the room

In an office, the lockers stand in the room where people work and hold meetings. That is why they have to look like part of the interior. Birch plywood is light and has an even surface. The doors can be oiled in a colour, e.g. dark grey or brown, and the carcass can stand in clear oil, so the layers of the plywood show as stripes on the edge. Handles are chosen in the designer, or the door can be without a handle and open with a push.

We draw the lockers to fit the room, so they can stand in a niche or along a corridor. A coat hook and a shelf in the compartment can be added.

faq.a: Nem Inventar makes office lockers to measure in birch and pine plywood and builds them in our own production. You can build the lockers in our [3D designer](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=locker) and see the price straight away, or send drawings to tilbud@neminventar.dk. We deliver and install throughout Denmark.

faq.q: Can office lockers have electronic locks?
faq.a: Yes. The lockers can have an electronic lock that opens with a tag or a card. 8 tall compartments in birch plywood with electronic locks, design handles and coat hooks cost [DKK 8,475 per compartment](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=locker&t=eyJzb2VqbGVyIjo0LCJyYWVra2VyIjoyLCJiIjo0MCwiaCI6OTAsImQiOjUwLCJtYXQiOiJiaXJrIiwiZnJvbnQiOiJmYXJ2ZSIsImZhcnZlIjp7ImxhYWdlIjoiY2hhcmNvYWwifSwiZ3JlYiI6Imx1a3N1cyIsImhhZW5nc2VsIjoibHVrc3VzIiwibGFhcyI6ImVsZWt0cm9uaXNrIiwia3JvZyI6Imtyb2cifQ) incl. VAT and DKK 6,780 excl. VAT in the designer.

faq.q: How much do office lockers cost?
faq.a: 16 compartments 35 cm wide and 45 cm high in birch plywood with code locks cost [DKK 3,000 per compartment](https://designer.neminventar.dk/designer?p=locker&t=eyJzb2VqbGVyIjo4LCJyYWVra2VyIjoyLCJiIjozNSwiaCI6NDUsImQiOjQ1LCJtYXQiOiJiaXJrIiwiaGFlbmdzZWwiOiJpbnN0aXR1dGlvbiIsImxhYXMiOiJrb2RlIn0) excl. VAT, DKK 48,000 excl. VAT in total, plus delivery. Tall compartments with electronic locks cost more, see the [price guide](/hvad-koster-lockers).

faq.q: How big should a compartment in an office locker be?
faq.a: For a bag and a laptop, a compartment 35 cm wide and 45 cm high is enough, and then there can be two tiers. If the jacket is to hang in the locker, choose a compartment 40 cm wide and 90 cm high with a coat hook.

faq.q: Can the lockers match the rest of the interior?
faq.a: Yes. The doors can be oiled in a colour, and the carcass can stand in clear oil, so the layers of the plywood show on the edge. From a sample or a RAL or NCS code, we find the closest colour.

faq.q: Do you deliver and install the lockers?
faq.a: Yes. We deliver throughout Denmark, carry the lockers in, put them up and adjust the doors. Delivery and installation are chosen in the designer's basket, and on a building project they are listed in the quote.
